title: Low-Voltage Foreman
description:
AMPAM is a leading Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing (MEP) contractor serving large-scale multifamily and commercial projects across California. With 1,500 employees across multiple business units, we are committed to delivering quality, safety, and excellence in every project. In June 2026, AMPAM acquired Coastal Fire & Integration Systems (“Coastal”), a San Diego-area provider of fire protection, low-voltage, and life safety systems. This role will join the AMPAM team as a part of our Coastal Fire & Integration Systems acquisition.

Brief Description: While the Inside Wireman/Installer is installing the wire and Homerun feeders on a project, the Foreman will be inspecting their work and addressing any issues with the work directly with the Wireman/Installer. The Foreman looks for problems that may occur during the construction process that relate to the scope of work he/she is responsible for. Typical work that the Foreman would be responsible for is installing the network of low voltage cabling that is used for video, voice and data, Fire Alarm or other low voltage signaling.

While most installations are in buildings that are partially or fully enclosed to protect from sun, wind and rain; these installations are often installed before air conditioning, heat or permanent light fixtures have been installed in the buildings. Many jobs, however, are in existing buildings or offices; and some work may be outside under varying weather conditions.

Backbone voice and data cables are routed between the entrance facility, where communications signals enter a building: to equipment rooms and telephone rooms. Voice and data horizontal cables are routed between telephone rooms or equipment rooms and individual workstations throughout the building. Equipment rooms often contain energized equipment such as hubs, file servers, electrical panels or telephone switches.

In some cases these devices are configured and connected to equipment that currently serves the building and must not be interrupted as a result of work performed by unqualified workers or those only partially trained. Any question of how a system goes together or works must be immediately brought to the attention of the foreman.

The Foreman oversees and participates in the installation voice, data, video and Fire Devices at the time of trim in their designated locations as identified on the approved plans/layouts. In addition, they install punch down blocks and cross connects in telephone rooms when required. These may be wall mounted or rack mounted, and must be grouped and identified according to specific installation standards. Whether the work is in new construction or in existing office or manufacturing space, the craftsman takes pride in the work he or she has and can performed. All testing required to insure the installation was done properly must be done to avoid return trips to do repairs or perform quality control work that should have already been completed.

Job Description: Many of the work processes of the Foreman are listed below. There are many systems that utilize low voltage voice, data, video and Fire Devices. Not all Foremen work on all systems. However, a properly trained Foreman can work on a variety of types of systems, including systems for voice, data, video and Fire Devices.

  • Plan and Initiate Projects at the Foreman level
  • Understand and follow the Building plans for the site adhering to all construction systems and regulations.
  • Install Underground voice, data, video and Fire Devices Feeders to Facilities
  • Determine Pathways, Hangers and Spaces for Installation of Low Voltage Wiring
  • Install, Terminate and Test Wires and Cables, both Copper and Fiber-Optic
  • Install, Test, Certify and Troubleshoot Local Area Network (LAN) Cabling Systems
  • Lay Out, Install and Verify Operation of Security and Access Control Systems
  • Install Communications and Sound Distribution Systems
  • Provide Testing, Analysis and Repair of Video, Voice and Data Systems; including Electronic Devices
  • Prefabricate Systems, such as Telecommunications Racks, for Field Installation

Foreman

Job Description continued:

  • Work on other Sub-systems such as Communications, Entertainment, Environmental, Fire Life Safety and Access Control.
  • Seal all penetrations through rated areas with approved Fire Stopping Methods.
  • Responsible for the filling out of their own timesheet correctly and getting it into the payroll dept. by the required time and day.
  • Verify the timesheets of all Wireman/Installers working for the foreman on his/her project that the work was carried out, complete and meets the industry standards for workmanship.
  • Attend production meetings hosted by the builders to more effectively manage the scope of work.
  • Develop relationships with the other trades as to improve the communication with said trades making our scope of work easier to accomplish.
  • Turn in meeting notes weekly.
  • Record all conversations pertaining to alterations in scope etc with a conversation record.
  • Maintain a red line set of plans of the job and turn them in at the jobs completion.
  • Line out the people assigned to his/her jobsite doing work in order to maintain an efficient completion of the work scope.
  • Maintain all safety requirements and immediately report those individuals not following the proper safety procedures.
  • Generate RFI’s to answer questions that need to be answered for us to complete our scope of work.
  • Order material for the job as per scope of work and insure it is onsite and available at the time of install.
  • Represent City-Wide in a professional manner and protect our interest.
  • Develop and train future Foremen and promote a positive work environment in which the Wireman/Installers may operate.

title: Intake Representative
description:
INTAKE REPRESENTATIVE

The Godsey Law Firm

You know how to take control of a difficult conversation without making the person on the other end feel controlled.

You stay calm when someone else is overwhelmed.

You hear the hesitation behind the words.

You know when to listen, when to ask another question, when to provide reassurance, and when it's time to confidently guide someone toward a decision.

If that describes you, your background may be exactly what we're looking for—even if you've never worked in a law firm.

THE ROLE

The Godsey Law Firm is a personal injury law firm seeking exceptional communicators to join our Intake Department.

Our Intake Representatives are often among the first people prospective clients speak with when they contact our Firm seeking information about potential representation.

These conversations matter.

A caller may have just been involved in an accident. They may be dealing with an injury, transportation problems, insurance questions, missed work, uncertainty about what happens next, or simply trying to determine whether they need an attorney.

Your responsibility is to listen, gather information, create clarity, build trust, explain our intake process accurately, address questions and concerns, and help qualified prospective clients make an informed decision about whether to move forward with our Firm.

This is not simply a customer service position.

It requires a rare combination of emotional intelligence, empathy, confidence, active listening, critical thinking, call control, resilience, and the ability to navigate objections and move conversations forward.

YOU MAY BE A GREAT FIT IF...

You have experience communicating with people during stressful, emotional, urgent, or high-stakes situations.

We are particularly interested in transferable experience from environments such as:

  • 911 or emergency communications/dispatch
  • Emergency or crisis response
  • Healthcare or patient intake
  • Hospital or emergency department registration
  • Insurance claims or claims intake
  • Roadside or emergency assistance
  • Victim services
  • Behavioral health or crisis-line intake
  • Customer retention
  • High-volume contact centers
  • Consultative sales
  • Other telephone-intensive environments requiring de-escalation, persuasion, judgment, or call control

Legal experience is not required.

We can teach you our systems, processes, and personal injury intake procedures.

We're looking for communication skills, judgment, emotional intelligence, resilience, and the ability to connect with people—qualities that are much harder to teach.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

As an Intake Representative, you will:

  • Handle a high volume of inbound and outbound telephone communications involving prospective clients who have contacted, been referred to, or otherwise engaged with the Firm regarding potential legal representation.
  • Speak professionally and compassionately with individuals who may be experiencing stress, frustration, uncertainty, or heightened emotions.
  • Establish rapport and trust quickly over the telephone.
  • Listen actively and ask thoughtful, structured questions to obtain relevant information.
  • Identify the concern behind a caller's hesitation or objection rather than simply relying on scripted responses.
  • Maintain appropriate control and direction of conversations while ensuring callers feel heard and respected.
  • Clearly and accurately explain the Firm's intake process and next steps.
  • Address prospective-client questions and concerns within the scope of your training and escalate matters when appropriate.
  • Help qualified prospective clients make informed decisions regarding moving forward with the Firm.
  • Confidently guide prospective clients who choose the Firm through the engagement and electronic contract process.
  • Conduct timely follow-up with prospective clients as appropriate and in accordance with Firm procedures.
  • Accurately document conversations, lead information, follow-up activity, and outcomes.
  • Work across multiple technology platforms while actively communicating with callers.
  • Meet established standards for call quality, responsiveness, documentation, follow-up, productivity, and qualified-lead conversion.
  • Follow all Firm policies, procedures, confidentiality requirements, ethical requirements, and applicable rules governing communications with prospective clients.

Intake Representatives do not provide legal advice or guarantee or predict the outcome or value of any potential case.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Emotional Intelligence

You recognize tone, hesitation, frustration, uncertainty, and other conversational cues and adjust your communication appropriately.

Genuine Empathy

You can make someone feel heard without losing focus on the purpose of the conversation.

Call Control

You can professionally redirect an emotional, resistant, highly talkative, or unfocused caller while maintaining rapport.

Active Listening

You don't simply wait for your turn to speak. You process what the person is telling you and use that information to determine what to ask or explain next.

Objection Navigation

When someone hesitates, you don't automatically push harder. You ask the right questions, identify the underlying concern, provide appropriate information, and help move the conversation toward resolution.

Confidence

You are comfortable asking for a decision after you've earned the right to do so.

Composure

You remain professional and effective when conversations become challenging.

Resilience

One difficult conversation doesn't affect your ability to deliver an exceptional experience on the next call.

Technology Agility

You are comfortable learning and simultaneously navigating multiple computer systems while communicating by telephone.

Results Orientation

You understand that providing an excellent prospective-client experience and achieving results can—and should—happen together.

BILINGUAL SKILLS

Bilingual English/Spanish communication skills are a plus, but are not required for this position.

Candidates are not required to be bilingual to be considered.

SCHEDULE & AVAILABILITY

Open availability is required for this position.

The Intake Department supports prospective-client communications across multiple shifts and days of the week. Candidates must be available to work mornings, afternoons, evenings/nights, and any day of the week, including weekends, based on business and staffing needs.

Current scheduling practices may include rotating schedules. The Firm may also assign employees to designated shifts based on operational needs.

A particular shift, schedule, day off, or permanent schedule is not guaranteed. Work schedules and shift assignments may be established or changed based on the operational and staffing needs of the Intake Department.

Candidates should apply only if they are able to maintain the scheduling flexibility required for the position.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

The Intake Representative position is fundamentally a telephone- and computer-based position. The following are essential functions of the job and must be performed with or without reasonable accommodation:

  • Regularly and consistently handle telephone communications throughout the scheduled workday.
  • Manage consecutive inbound and outbound calls as required by call volume and operational needs.
  • Communicate clearly and effectively by telephone with prospective clients and others.
  • Listen to, comprehend, process, and respond to information during live conversations.
  • Maintain appropriate attention and concentration during telephone communications.
  • Simultaneously communicate with callers, gather information, review information, enter data, and navigate Firm systems.
  • Operate a computer and related office technology throughout the scheduled workday.
  • Regularly use a keyboard, mouse, telephone/headset, and other standard office equipment.
  • Continuously access and navigate electronic information necessary to perform intake responsibilities.
  • Frequently transition among multiple computer applications, browser windows, communication platforms, databases, electronic documents, and other Firm technologies.
  • Accurately enter, retrieve, review, and document information electronically.
  • Perform real-time or timely documentation of prospective-client communications and outcomes.
  • Exercise sound judgment, active listening, problem-solving, call control, and appropriate escalation during telephone interactions.
  • Professionally communicate with individuals who may be emotional, distressed, frustrated, confused, skeptical, or resistant.
  • Maintain confidentiality and appropriately handle sensitive information.
  • Consistently perform assigned intake, follow-up, documentation, and prospective-client communication responsibilities within established timeframes.
  • Maintain reliable attendance and availability sufficient to perform assigned responsibilities and provide scheduled Intake Department coverage.

PHYSICAL AND WORK ENVIRONMENT

This is primarily a sedentary, telephone- and computer-intensive office position.

The position generally involves:

  • Performing work from an assigned workstation for the substantial majority of the workday.
  • Sitting for prolonged periods while performing telephone and computer-based responsibilities.
  • Frequent and repetitive use of a computer keyboard and mouse.
  • Frequent use of telephone/headset equipment.
  • Viewing and processing information displayed on computer monitors throughout the workday.
  • Frequent switching between computer applications and electronic systems.
  • Simultaneously using telephone and computer technology.
  • Working in an environment where telephone communications occur throughout the scheduled workday.

The physical and work-environment requirements described above represent the manner in which the essential functions of this position are ordinarily performed. Qualified individuals must be able to perform the essential functions of the position with or without reasonable accommodation.

WHY INTAKE MATTERS

Intake isn't simply about answering a telephone.

It is where someone searching for help first experiences The Godsey Law Firm.

The way you listen matters.

The questions you ask matter.

The trust you build matters.

And your ability to help someone move from uncertainty to an informed decision matters.

If you're exceptional at connecting with people, controlling complex telephone conversations, navigating resistance, and turning uncertainty into action, we want to hear from you.

EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY

The Godsey Law Firm provides equal employment opportunities to qualified applicants and employees and does not discriminate on the basis of any characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Reasonable accommodations are available to qualified individuals with disabilities in accordance with applicable law. Applicants who require a reasonable accommodation to participate in the application or selection process may request one through the Firm's Human Resources Department.

The Godsey Law Firm reserves the right to modify job duties, schedules, and assignments based on business needs, consistent with applicable law.

The Logistics Management Specialist supports Army enterprise readiness by providing operational and strategic analysis of equipping, modernization, force readiness, and sustainment programs. Contingent Upon Contract Award

Duties & Responsibilities

  • Analyze Army equipping guidance, modernization programs, and readiness requirements across the logistics enterprise.
  • Coordinate logistics synchronization activities among AMC, ACOMs, ASCCs, DRUs, and HQDA stakeholders.
  • Support readiness initiatives including Fleet Management Expansion (FMX), Total Army Readiness Reviews (TARR), Strategic Readiness Assessments, and Focused Unit Readiness programs.
  • Evaluate materiel readiness trends and identify deficiencies affecting operational capability.
  • Develop executive briefings, dashboards, reports, and decision-support products for senior leaders.
  • Analyze logistics and maintenance data utilizing GCSS-A, Decision Support Tool (DST), and other enterprise systems.
  • Recommend improvements to readiness reporting, equipment management, and sustainment processes.
  • Support planning and execution of force modernization and equipment distribution initiatives.
  • Facilitate meetings, working groups, and stakeholder engagements involving operational readiness and logistics sustainment.
  • Monitor Army readiness metrics and assess impacts of policy, funding, and operational decisions.
  • Prepare analyses supporting strategic logistics and sustainment planning efforts.

  • Bachelor's Degree in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Business Management, Engineering, or related field.
  • Minimum ten (10) years of Army logistics experience at the Brigade level or higher.
  • Minimum five (5) years supporting ACOM, ASCC, Theater Army, Corps, or HQDA organizations.
  • Demonstrated experience with GCSS-A, DST, Army readiness reporting systems, and logistics analytics.
  • Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel, SharePoint, and Power BI or equivalent business intelligence tools.
  • Experience preparing and presenting information to senior Army leaders.
  • Must be a U.S. Citizen and have an Active Secret security clearance.

The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this position include close vision, distance vision, and the ability to adjust focus. The noise level in the work environment is typically low to moderate.

title: Seasonal Ridgerunner (Great Smoky Mountains)
description:
Organizational Mission:

The Appalachian Trail Conservancy’s mission is to protect, manage, and advocate for the Appalachian National Scenic Trail.

Position Summary


ATC Ridgerunners provide information about the A.T. and its intended primitive experience, location, regulations, and traditions. They work to encourage the best behavior on the part of hikers to facilitate a positive Trail experience (particularly for those who are poorly prepared), and to elicit the support of those who live nearby. They discourage and mitigate misuse of the Appalachian Trail and its environments by performing educational and public-relations functions.

Ridgerunners are assigned to hike specific sections of the A.T. during the day and camp at specific, high-use overnight sites throughout their patrol. Applicants should demonstrate the interest and ability to contribute to the public service effort of working on a National Scenic Trail and to promote volunteerism and membership in ATC and its club affiliates. They should possess the required skills listed below and be able to attend required trainings. Applicants must demonstrate maturity, responsibility, initiative, and self-motivation.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Meet and greet the public and educate them about the A.T., the ATC, local Trail Clubs, local land agencies and Leave No Trace practices.
  • Advise visitors on rules and regulations pertinent to the A.T. in the Smokies, including general backcountry and thru-hiker permits, proper food storage, and when relevant, parking tag requirements.
  • Perform minor Trail maintenance which includes but not limited to, picking up litter on the Trail, overnight sites, and at Trailhead parking areas.
  • Assist with privy maintenance as needed.
  • Assist visitors, and when necessary and able, aid in emergency response incidents.
  • Report unsafe conditions, misuse, and abuse of the A.T. and its overnight facilities.
  • Maintain regular contact with field supervisors, Club volunteers, agency partners, and local officials.
  • Complete a summary report at the end of each work period and attend a weekly debrief call with supervisors and partners.
  • Regularly traverse steep and uneven terrain in all weather conditions, traveling upwards of 15 miles daily, while carrying approximately 30 pounds.

Qualifications

  • Commitment to Trail and resource protection efforts.
  • Proven ability to work alone with minimal supervision.
  • Ability to effectively communicate with individuals and groups.
  • Strong backpacking and outdoor experience.
  • Experience in working with volunteers of all ages, backgrounds, and skill levels.
  • Ability to hike up to 10 miles per day in steep, mountainous terrain.
  • Basic knowledge of Long Trail/Appalachian Trail system preferred.
  • Leave No Trace Trainer or Master Educator desirable, but training provided.
  • Current First-Aid and CPR certification (Wilderness First-Aid certification is preferable) training can be provided.
  • Previous A.T. volunteer experience is a preferred.

Physical Demands and Work Environment

  • Regular use of a computer is required; Microsoft Office, Office 365, ESRI GIS, NPS database and Google applications are used.
  • May be exposed to hazardous physical conditions and seasonal exposure to extreme weather conditions, including rain, snow, humidity, intense heat, and sunlight.
  • Must be able to hike for extended periods, stand for long periods, perform routine moderate lifting, carry up to 50 pounds in a backpack over a minimum of five miles, traverse rough, uneven terrain and wet and slippery surfaces.
  • Living and performing work in the backcountry for multiple days and overnights.
  • Must have valid driver’s license. Access to a personal vehicle is strongly preferred.
  • Possible exposure to ticks and pests, extreme weather, and hazards typical of a backcountry environment
  • Long days in the field and weekend work, typically 40 hours per week

Additional Details:

  • ATC is hiring two short-season Ridgerunners (February 22, 2027 to June 28, 2027) and one long-season Ridgerunner (February 22, 2027 to October 25, 2027)
  • While Ridgerunners in the Smokies are ATC employees, they will have a close working relationship with Great Smoky Mountains National Park and Smoky Mountains Hiking Club.
  • Hourly Rate: $19.00 - $21.00
  • Location/Region required to work from: Great Smoky Mountains National Park.
  • Benefits: 1 hour of sick time per 30 hours worked.
  • A field food stipend will be offered.
  • Smokies Ridgerunners have the option of staying in free, provided housing near Gatlinburg, TN.
  • Reliable access to a personal vehicle is required. Mileage will be reimbursed at the federal rate.

Huntsville, AL

Since its inception, RBCI has made a concerted effort to attract and recruit talented individuals from all walks of life. RBCI is a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) providing information technology (IT) services and solutions, and professional services to commercial businesses, the Department of Defense (DoD), and other federal agencies.

RBCI provides generous benefits to our employees, including health/dental insurance, short-term/long-term disability, and a 401(K)-retirement plan, in addition to a highly competitive salary.

For more information, please visit us at www.rbci.com.

Position Summary

The Operations Research Systems Analyst (ORSA) serves as AMC's advanced analytics and decision-support expert, applying quantitative methodologies, predictive modeling, simulation techniques, and optimization strategies to complex logistics, readiness, modernization, and force structure challenges. The ORSA develops analytical products that enable senior Army leaders to evaluate alternatives, mitigate risk, improve readiness, and optimize resource allocation across the Army enterprise.

The work for this position shall be performed onsite in Huntsville, Alabama.

Contingent Upon Contract Award

Duties & Responsibilities

The essential and specific functions include but are not limited to the following:

  • Conduct advanced statistical analyses, operations research studies, predictive modeling, simulation, and optimization assessments.
  • Analyze readiness, equipping, modernization, and sustainment data to identify trends and develop recommendations.
  • Perform equipment gap analyses supporting Army modernization and rapid equipping efforts.
  • Develop analytical models supporting force structure development, logistics optimization, and resource allocation decisions.
  • Utilize Vantage, DST, R Studio, SACS, and other analytical tools to examine operational and logistics performance.
  • Design and execute quantitative studies evaluating courses of action and operational outcomes.
  • Assess operational risks, readiness impacts, and sustainment challenges using data-driven methodologies.
  • Prepare technical reports, executive briefings, decision papers, and recommendations for senior Army leadership.
  • Present analytical results to General Officers, senior executives, and strategic stakeholders.
  • Support Army studies, experimentation efforts, modernization initiatives, and strategic planning activities.
  • Provide subject matter expertise to working groups, integrated planning teams, and senior decision forums.

Qualifications

  • Master's Degree in Operations Research, Mathematics, Statistics, Data Science, Engineering, Economics, or related quantitative discipline.
  • Minimum fifteen (15) years of experience applying advanced analytical methods to military, logistics, readiness, or business problems.
  • Minimum five (5) years supporting Army rapid acquisition, rapid equipping, or modernization requirements.
  • Minimum five (5) years conducting equipment gap analyses and readiness assessments.
  • Experience with Vantage, DST, R Studio, SACS, statistical analysis, simulation, and predictive modeling techniques.
  • Experience supporting AMC, HQDA G-4, Army Futures Command, or Army modernization organizations.
  • Demonstrated experience briefing General Officers and SES-level leadership.
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate complex analytical findings to senior leaders.
  • Must be a U.S. Citizen and have an Active Secret security clearance.

Physical Demands and Work Environment

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the functions. While performing the duties of this position, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to use hands or fingers, handle or feel objects, tools, or controls. The employee is occasionally required to stand; walk; sit; and reach with hands and arms. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this position include close vision, distance vision, and the ability to adjust focus. The noise level in the work environment is typically low to moderate.

Note

This job description in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by the employee(s) incumbent in this position. Employees will be required to follow any other job-related instructions and to perform any other job-related duties requested by any person authorized to give instructions or assignments. title: Senior Product Manager
description:
Senior Product Manager

Life @ AP+:

We are one connected team in pursuit of one inspiring purpose – to unite people and technology to power better experiences. Each of us has a part to play in making that happen. You’ll be encouraged to bring your big ideas forward and make a difference through your work. Taking steps forward in your career whilst still having room for fun, friendships, and flexibility in your daily life.

We’re driven by our core values: lead with heart, learn for tomorrow and live our legacy. A purpose like ours takes the inspired impact of an incredible team. Ready to change the game? We’re ready to help you do it.

The Purpose

As a Senior Product Manager for Merchants and Online products within our AP+ Retail Payments team, you’ll take end-to-end accountability for retail products in online payment channels across their full lifecycle, shaping propositions, roadmaps and delivery to meet customer needs and strategic objectives. You’ll combine market insight, user feedback and performance data with strong stakeholder leadership to guide decisions, deliver change and continually evolve products within Australia’s payments ecosystem.

Key Responsibilities the Role Owns:

  • Formulate a clear product definition and strategy for eftpos card-not-present products including identifying opportunities to strengthen eftpos' relevance, customer value and sustainable competitive advantage in online payments.
  • Lead product through the full product lifecycle from inception and proposition development through launch, growth, optimisation and retirement.
  • Gather and communicate customer, market, stakeholder and product performance insights on trends, needs and risks to shape product propositions, positioning, priorities and development.
  • Develop business cases and inform investment decisions through opportunity sizing, feasibility assessment, financial modelling, risk analysis and strategic alignment.
  • Define product roadmap and work with product owner(s) to detail product requirements and priorities based on business objectives and customer value.
  • Collaborate with Scheme and Commercial Teams to define the go-to-market strategy, helping them understand the product positioning, key benefits, and target customer.
  • You’ll likely be a strong fit for this role if:
  • You have 5+ years of product management experience with a focus on card payments and e-commerce.
  • You’ve shaped product propositions and roadmaps using market research, user insight, feedback and product performance data.
  • You have proven experience developing and commercialising eCommerce payment products or services, ideally involving acquirers, payment service providers and merchants, with a strong understanding of how these participants interact across the online payments value chain
  • You bring strong customer and stakeholder management, with proven ability to influence and communicate with stakeholders across the value chain as well as commercial, marketing and delivery teams. You’re confident developing business cases, translating strategy into clear product outcomes and influencing senior stakeholders through evidence-based advice.
  • You bring strong knowledge of payments products, technology, and the financial industry, supported by relevant tertiary qualifications or equivalent industry experience.

What happens next:

At AP+, we believe in the power of passion, pride and purpose. Our team is driven by a shared mission to make a difference in the world of payments, and we're proud to work together towards this common goal.

If you’re a senior product leader who thrives on complex problems, meaningful stakeholder influence and shaping products that sit at the heart of Australia’s payments ecosystem, we’d love to hear from you.

If you’re ready to be a game changer, please submit your application. The Talent Acquisition team will endeavour to review your application and notify you of the outcome within the next two weeks.

We want to remove all barriers to inclusion, so if you need advice or support with your application, we’re here to help. Please reach out to recruitment@auspayplus.com.au. We also encourage you to let us know your pronouns at any point during the recruitment process.

AP+ are not partnering with Recruitment agencies for this role.

title: Lead Integration Architect
description:
Intelance is appointing a Lead Integration Architect as a contract associate for the definition phase of a major UK enterprise technology programme. You will work directly with Intelance's Chief Enterprise Architect and a small senior team. The work will define how legacy, Oracle, operational, reporting and external systems should exchange information through a controlled integration platform. This is a hands on architecture role. The expected commitment is about 28 days across an 8 to 10 week period. Delivery will be mainly remote, with limited planned travel where needed.

Tasks

  • Verify the existing connections between Oracle, bespoke applications, reporting tools and external services.
  • Produce an accurate current integration map and identify the connections that create the greatest risk or effort.
  • Design the target integration architecture and the rules that all future connections should follow.
  • Define the priority connections and the order in which they should move.
  • Lead the technical requirements and assessment for the integration platform.
  • Define practical patterns for APIs, events, files, scheduled transfers, monitoring and error handling.
  • Work closely with the Oracle Technical Architect and Security Architect.
  • Estimate the delivery effort, skills, dependencies and technical risks for each stage.
  • Produce clear diagrams and decision papers for senior business and technology leaders.
  • Provide a clean handover into implementation.

Requirements

  • At least 10 years of technology architecture experience.
  • Strong recent experience leading enterprise integration architecture.
  • Evidence from at least three programmes involving ERP, Oracle, bespoke applications or complex legacy systems.
  • Practical experience replacing direct system connections with a managed integration approach.
  • Strong knowledge of APIs, messaging, event based integration, file transfer and batch processing.
  • Experience assessing integration platforms and implementation partners.
  • Able to turn incomplete technical information into clear decisions, costs and delivery steps.
  • Able to create simple executive diagrams and detailed technical designs.
  • Clear written and spoken English.
  • Based in the United Kingdom, with the right to work in the United Kingdom.
  • Available for about 28 days across an 8 to 10 week period.

Experience in manufacturing, distribution or supply chain businesses is useful. Experience with Oracle estates is also useful. No single integration platform is required because the platform has not yet been selected.

Benefits

  • £575 to £650 per day, depending on directly relevant experience.
  • Flexible delivery pattern across the agreed 8 to 10 week period.
  • Direct access to Intelance's Chief Enterprise Architect and senior client decision makers.
  • A clearly defined piece of work with named outputs and decision points.
  • Potential follow on architecture and delivery work, subject to programme approval and performance.
  • Pre agreed travel expenses paid separately.

Please apply with a current CV. The process is a short screening form, a 30 minute introductory call and one focused technical discussion. We will move quickly and keep the process clear. The engagement will be subject to contract, reference checks and an IR35 status assessment.

title: Lab Assistant
description:
Certified Group is committed to partnering with customers to deliver innovative scientific solutions and expertise – So The World Can Trust In What It Consumes™. Our network of 30+ North American and European laboratories serves the food & beverage, dietary supplements, cosmetics, OTC, tobacco/nicotine, cannabis, and hemp industries.

Our Brands

Certified Group is comprised of a set of specialized brands that collectively deliver laboratory testing, regulatory consulting, and certification & audit services across highly regulated industries:

  • Certified Laboratories – Provides comprehensive analytical and microbiological testing, primarily supporting food, beverage, cosmetics, OTC, and dietary supplement industries.
  • Food Safety Net Services (FSNS) – A leading network of ISO-accredited laboratories across North America, focused on food safety testing, operational support, and technical services for the food industry.
  • Labstat – A global leader in contract research and testing for nicotine, tobacco, cannabis, hemp, and next-generation products, with deep expertise in analytical chemistry and toxicology.
  • EAS Consulting Group – A regulatory consulting firm offering expert guidance, training, and auditing support across FDA, USDA, and other regulated sectors, powered by a large network of independent advisors.
  • FSNS Certification & Audit – Provides accredited third-party auditing and certification services, including food safety, animal welfare, and GMP programs.

We are currently looking for a Lab Assistant to join our growing team!

Essential Responsibilities

• Logging of customer samples into the LIMS system with accuracy. Uses products as needed.
• Split samples between department

• Provides proactive customer service to include contacting customers via phone, email, video chat and other means to communicate relevant information and updates about their testing.
• Ensure timeliness, accuracy, and reliability work.
• Ensure adherence to the daily work schedule.
• Make suggestions and recommendations regarding product/specs. that would aid in logging, including communication with customers.
• Perform clerical review to ensure accuracy.
• Ensure all samples are labeled correctly and stored at the appropriate temperatures until testing can occur.
• Ensure the sample receiving/splitting room is cleaned and maintained.
• Participate in special projects as assigned by the Manager/Supervisor.
• Keep the Manager/Supervisor informed of issues or problems within the department.
• Interact with clients, suppliers and vendors as required.
• Learn new techniques and technologies and trains others as appropriate.
• Work effectively with other departments.
• Responsible for the execution of all ISO and QC requirements.
• Stock/order supplies as needed (labels, boxes etc.)
• Assist with sample retain and retrieval
• Assists with purchasing and inventory
• Assist in media prep
• Assist in cleaning of laboratory glassware
• Assist in general laboratory housekeeping tasks
• Other duties as required.

Education & Experience

• High school diploma
• Knowledge of good aseptic technique and behaviors that can reduce cross contamination.
• Good conceptual basis in laboratory setting with proven ability to perform basic lab techniques.
• Critical thinking – using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions or approaches to problems.
• Excellent organizational skills - ability to use your time, energy, resources, etc. in an effective manner.
• Time management – one’s own time and the time of others.
• Training – teaching and guiding others how to complete a process from beginning to end.
• Strong relevant qualitative and quantitative skills.
• Excellent arithmetic skills – using mathematics to solve problems.
• Good communication skills – speaking, reading, writing and listening.
• Manual dexterity.
• Ability to stand for prolonged periods and lift up to 40 lbs.

Skills & Competencies

  • Strong organizational skills and ability to complete detailed manual tasks.
  • Ability to work under deadlines, manage interruptions, and multitask effectively.
  • Logical thinking and accuracy in task completion.
  • Basic math skills: add, subtract, multiply, divide, and work with fractions and decimals.
  • Ability to follow written and oral instructions and problem-solve within standardized situations.
  • Working knowledge of ISO 17025 quality procedures and general OSHA laboratory safety guidelines preferred.

Physical Demands & Work Environment

  • Frequent standing, walking, sitting, reaching, and handling of materials.
  • Occasional stooping, kneeling, crouching, or crawling.
  • Regular use of hands and fingers to operate laboratory equipment and computers.
  • Ability to lift and/or move up to 25 pounds.
  • Potential exposure to odors, fumes, airborne particles, hazardous chemicals, and microbiological pathogens.
  • Varying noise levels and temperatures (hot to cold).
  • Fast-paced, team-oriented environment.
  • Overnight travel may be required at the discretion of management.
  • Must wear appropriate protective clothing and equipment.

General Requirements

  • Flexible schedule availability.
  • Ability to perform opening and closing procedures in the media laboratory.
  • Commitment to workplace safety for self and others.
  • Willingness to work as part of a collaborative, team-driven environment.

title: Construction Project Manager
description:
We are seeking for a Project Manager who is responsible for the successful execution and delivery of assigned IRTH Contracting projects in accordance with the contract, approved scope, programme, budget, quality, HSSE and authority requirements.

The role has direct responsibility for organising project resources, coordinating construction activities, managing subcontractors and ensuring that drawings, materials, labour, plant, approvals and work fronts are available when required.

The Project Manager acts as the primary coordination point between the project execution team and the central Planning, Cost Control, Procurement, Commercial & Contracts, Design and Engineering, MEP, QA/QC and HSSE functions.

Requirements

Project Planning and Mobilisation

  • Review the contract, scope, drawings, specifications, programme, budget and project requirements.
  • Establish the project execution plan, organisation structure, responsibility matrix and communication procedures.
  • Coordinate mobilisation of project personnel, subcontractors, temporary facilities, permits, plant, equipment and site services.
  • Identify critical activities, long-lead items, project risks and execution constraints at an early stage.
  • Establish clear project objectives, priorities and performance expectations.
  • Ensure that required approvals, insurances, securities, permits and project documentation are in place.

Construction Execution

  • Lead the day-to-day execution and coordination of the project from mobilisation through completion.
  • Ensure that works are executed in accordance with approved drawings, specifications, method statements and programmes.
  • Coordinate civil, structural, architectural, MEP and specialist works.
  • Ensure that sufficient labour, supervision, materials, plant and work fronts are available.
  • Monitor productivity, sequencing and resource utilisation and implement corrective measures where required.
  • Chair regular project progress, coordination and performance meetings.
  • Resolve site constraints promptly and escalate matters requiring senior-management intervention.
  • Prevent unauthorised work, commitments or deviations from approved project requirements.
  • Maintain accurate records of progress, instructions, changes, delays, risks and decisions.

Programme and Progress Management

  • Coordinate with Planning in developing and maintaining the baseline programme, detailed schedules and look-ahead plans.
  • Monitor actual progress against contractual and internal milestones.
  • Ensure that site priorities and resource requirements are aligned with the approved programme.
  • Identify delays, critical-path impacts and emerging constraints at an early stage.
  • Develop and implement recovery measures where progress falls behind programme.
  • Ensure that reported progress accurately reflects actual site conditions.
  • Provide records and information required for delay analysis, contractual notices and extension-of-time submissions.

Cost and Budget Coordination

  • Coordinate with Cost Control on project budgets, commitments, actual expenditure, forecasts and cost-to-complete.
  • Ensure that project expenditure and resource decisions remain within approved budgets and authority levels.
  • Monitor labour, material, plant and subcontractor costs and identify adverse trends.
  • Support the preparation of realistic project forecasts based on current site conditions and remaining work.
  • Implement corrective and cost-recovery measures where budget pressures or cost overruns are identified.
  • Ensure that project information required for cost reporting is complete, accurate and submitted on time.
  • Prevent unauthorised expenditure or commitments.

Procurement and Materials Coordination

  • Coordinate project procurement requirements and priorities with the Projects Control Director and Procurement team.
  • Ensure that material requisitions include accurate quantities, specifications, drawings, approvals and required-on-site dates.
  • Monitor material submissions, technical evaluations, purchase orders, manufacturing, inspections and deliveries.
  • Identify long-lead materials and procurement risks at an early stage.
  • Coordinate with Design, MEP, QA/QC and Procurement to resolve technical or approval-related delays.
  • Monitor delivery schedules and escalate delays that may affect construction progress.
  • Ensure that delivered materials are properly received, inspected, stored, protected and recorded.
  • Support alternative sourcing and recovery measures where required.

Subcontractor Management

  • Coordinate the mobilisation, performance and delivery of subcontractors.
  • Ensure that subcontractors provide adequate supervision, labour, plant, materials and technical resources.
  • Monitor subcontractor progress, productivity, quality, HSSE compliance and adherence to programme.
  • Ensure that subcontractors work within their approved scope and contractual requirements.
  • Identify underperformance and require corrective or recovery plans.
  • Coordinate with Commercial & Contracts, Procurement, QA/QC and HSSE regarding delays, defective work, non-compliance, back-charges or payment matters.
  • Recommend suspension, replacement or other contractual action where serious underperformance continues.
  • Verify subcontractor progress and completed work for payment-assessment purposes.

Commercial and Contractual Coordination

  • Understand the project’s contractual obligations, milestones, notice requirements and payment provisions.
  • Coordinate with Commercial & Contracts regarding correspondence, valuations, variations, claims and subcontract matters.
  • Ensure that instructions, changes, delays, additional works and access restrictions are properly recorded.
  • Provide timely site records supporting contractual notices, variations, claims and extensions of time.
  • Prevent unauthorised scope changes, commitments or contractual concessions.
  • Support the measurement and valuation of completed work.
  • Assist with the timely submission and certification of interim payment applications.
  • Support the preparation, negotiation and agreement of the project final account.

Design, Technical and MEP Coordination

  • Coordinate with Design and Engineering, Technical and MEP teams to ensure the timely release of coordinated construction information.
  • Monitor drawings, RFIs, technical submissions, material approvals and design changes.
  • Identify incomplete information, design conflicts and constructability issues before they affect progress.
  • Ensure effective coordination between civil, architectural, structural, MEP and specialist systems.
  • Ensure that approved design changes are communicated to all affected parties.
  • Prevent construction using superseded, unapproved or incomplete information.
  • Coordinate technical solutions that meet contractual, construction and operational requirements

.

Quality, HSSE and Compliance

  • Ensure that all project activities comply with approved Quality and HSSE plans.
  • Hold project personnel and subcontractors accountable for safe working practices and required quality standards.
  • Ensure that work does not proceed without approved drawings, method statements, risk assessments, permits and competent supervision.
  • Support QA/QC in preventing defects, rework and the use of unapproved materials.
  • Ensure timely closure of non-conformances, inspection findings and corrective actions.
  • Support HSSE personnel in stopping unsafe activities and implementing immediate corrective measures.
  • Ensure compliance with authority, environmental, labour-welfare and site-security requirements.
  • Promote a project culture based on safety, quality, accountability and early problem resolution.

Stakeholder Management and Reporting

  • Act as the main project representative for the client, consultant, subcontractors and internal departments.
  • Maintain professional relationships while protecting IRTH Contracting’s contractual and commercial interests.
  • Provide accurate and timely reports covering progress, programme, cost, procurement, quality, HSSE and project risks.
  • Clearly identify matters requiring decisions, approvals or senior-management intervention.
  • Manage stakeholder expectations and ensure that commitments are realistic and properly authorised.
  • Escalate material delays, disputes, compliance failures and performance concerns to the Projects Director.
  • Ensure that meeting minutes, action registers and project records remain current and properly controlled.

Testing, Handover and Close-Out

  • Plan and coordinate testing, commissioning, authority inspections, snagging and handover activities.
  • Ensure timely completion of as-built drawings, operation and maintenance manuals, warranties, certificates and handover records.
  • Monitor closure of outstanding works, defects and contractual deliverables.
  • Coordinate phased handover, operational readiness and transfer of completed areas where applicable.
  • Ensure the proper protection of completed works until formal handover.
  • Coordinate orderly demobilisation of personnel, temporary facilities, plant and materials.
  • Participate in project close-out reviews and document lessons learned.

Team Leadership

  • Lead and coordinate the assigned project execution team.
  • Establish clear responsibilities, objectives and performance expectations.
  • Monitor team capability, workload, productivity and conduct.
  • Identify staffing, training and specialist-support requirements.
  • Coordinate site priorities with central functional departments while respecting their reporting structures.
  • Hold team members accountable for timely action, accurate reporting and compliance with company procedures.
  • Promote collaboration, professional integrity, ownership and effective communication.

Benefits

  • Private Health Insurance
  • Performance Bonus
  • Annual air ticket allowance
  • Family Benefits

At IRTH Group, we’re not just a company; we’re a family committed to building a brighter future together. Guided by our core values of trust, strength, and agility, we empower individuals to thrive and succeed in a dynamic, collaborative environment. We take pride in building great projects in prime locations, designed for future generations and offering exceptional value as an investor's product. IRTH Group stands as a symbol of legacy, resilience, and vision. Rooted in the foundation of a distinguished local family conglomerate, our privately held real estate investment platform draws strength from a heritage spanning over a century.

At IRTH Group, we are not just shaping the industry, we are setting the standard. If you are driven by ambition, excellence, and the pursuit of legacy, this is where your journey begins.

title: Senior Director, Analytics Engineering, Data Analytics & AI
description:
At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.

Snowflake is about empowering enterprises to achieve their full potential with Data & AI. With a culture that's all in on impact, innovation, and collaboration, Snowflake is the sweet spot for building big, moving fast, and taking technology and careers to the next level.

We're hiring for a Senior Director of Analytics Engineering to join our Data, Analytics, and AI organization (DAA), reporting directly to the Chief Data & Analytics Officer. You will lead a team of 20+ Analytics Engineers that build and operate the pipelines behind Snowflake's revenue, bookings, people analytics, and go-to-market reporting within our governed data platform.

This role has an in-office requirement — you must be able to work out of our Menlo Park office a minimum of 3 days a week.

In This Role You Will

  • Lead and grow the Analytics Engineering organization: Manage through your direct reports (team leads/managers), setting priorities and technical strategy across the team.

  • Drive Snowflake’s internal data transformation: Lead your teams' ongoing work to create an AI ready data foundation, with an emphasis on documentation, contracts, context, and governance.

  • Own Snowflake’s internal analytics agents: Build, improve, and maintain general purpose analytics agents - and underlying context and semantic layers - that can be used across the organization including evals, orchestration instructions, and ground truth data sets

  • Champion AI-assisted engineering: Drive adoption of Cortex Code-based agentic workflows and reusable skills across your teams to speed up typical Analytics Engineering jobs-to-be-done, including model development, PR review, and root-cause analysis.

  • Act as Snowflake’s customer zero: Be the first trusted tester of Snowflake’s own features across the data engineering and transformation stack, deeply engaging with Product and Engineering teams on product and feature roadmaps

  • Represent Snowflake: Support our GTM and Frontier Engineering teams by joining customer conversations, supporting speaking engagements, and publishing thought leadership, ultimately demonstrating the art of possible on Snowflake to all our customers and prospects

  • Continually push our stack forward: Push the boundaries of what we can accomplish on Snowflake, adopting the latest internal Data and AI capabilities.

  • Partner cross-functionally: Serve as the primary point of escalation for business stakeholders, driving towards a common roadmap and transforming upstream processes and workflows with data in mind

  • Represent your teams upward and cross-org: Contribute your teams' patterns and learnings to the Data, Analytics, and AI org's broader technical initiatives

What You Will Need

  • 10+ years of experience in analytics engineering, data engineering, or data architecture, including second line leadership experience managing managers or senior individual contributors across multiple teams.

  • A systems thinker at your core: You naturally see how individual data models, pipelines, and architectural decisions connect — and you design for second-order effects, not just the immediate problem.

  • Deep expertise in Snowflake, including data modeling, data governance (e.g., RBAC design, row access policies and masking policies), and the broader Snowflake feature set (Dynamic Tables, Streams, Tasks, Horizon, Cortex)

  • Expert-level dbt skills, including macro development, testing and CI/CD frameworks, and large-scale multi-team project management.

  • Hands-on experience with Airflow or similar orchestration platforms

  • A track record owning finance- or revenue-critical, deadline-driven data pipelines where accuracy and auditability are non-negotiable.

  • Familiarity with GTM and sales analytics domains: master data management, consumption & attainment pipelines, quota/territory data.

  • Advanced adoption of AI-assisted engineering tools — Cortex Code, Claude Code, or similar agent frameworks — including agentic skill development and prompt engineering for data workflows.

  • A record of driving large scale data transformation initiatives across complex organizations

  • Experience with downstream BI/consumption layers such as Streamlit, Sigma, Tableau, etc.

  • Comfort working in a Jira/Confluence-based agile delivery model.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a track record of writing clear technical specs and stakeholder-facing materials for non-technical audiences

Snowflake employees must abide by the company’s data security plan as an essential part of their duties. It is every employee's duty to keep customer information secure and confidential.

location: Youth Housing Program, Edmonton, AB, CA
description:
About e4c

e4c journeys with people as they shape the lives they envision, building resources, relationships, and belonging in the communities they call home. Guided by our vision of a community where every person has the opportunity to live with dignity, belonging, and purpose, we deliver person-led, collaborative, and evidence-informed services that strengthen individuals, families, and communities. Rooted in our core values of courage, compassion, connection, and commitment, we are dedicated to creating lasting opportunities and meaningful community impact.

Position Summary

The Youth Housing Program provides Community Group Care for youth aged 13–17 with complex needs, offering trauma-informed, developmentally responsive, and therapeutic care in a safe and supportive home environment.

As the Overnight Lead, you will support the safety, well-being, and development of youth through individualized care, relationship-based practice, and case management. Working collaboratively with each youth's Care Team, you will foster their physical, emotional, mental, and spiritual well-being while ensuring a safe, clean, and supportive home environment. The Overnight Lead provides day-to-day guidance, coaching, and support to Support Workers, helping ensure quality service delivery, operational consistency, and the successful completion of overnight responsibilities.

Schedule

  • 4 days on 2 days off rotation; 11:30PM – 8:00AM
  • This is a shift working position and schedule may vary according to program needs.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead and support the safety, well-being, and development of youth by promoting individualized care, healthy routines, and trauma-informed, relationship-based practices.
  • Build trusting relationships with youth using active listening, strengths-based approaches, crisis intervention, and de-escalation techniques to promote safety and positive outcomes.
  • Guide Youth Workers and Support Workers in implementing individualized care plans, case management strategies, and goal-oriented supports for youth.
  • Oversee the delivery of direct care, including wellness checks, medication administration, daily routines, and interventions that promote physical, emotional, mental, and spiritual well-being.
  • Ensure a safe, clean, and well-maintained home environment by overseeing household operations, safety inspections, inventory, documentation, and compliance with licensing, accreditation, and occupational health and safety standards.
  • Provide day-to-day leadership, coaching, supervision, and performance feedback to Support Workers while fostering a collaborative, trauma-informed team environment.
  • Coordinate staff assignments, monitor training requirements, and support employee development to ensure consistent, high-quality service delivery.
  • Oversee critical incident reporting, documentation, follow-up actions, and quality improvement initiatives while ensuring compliance with organizational policies and procedures.
  • Participate in the on-call rotation, providing leadership and after-hours support during crises, staff absences, and other operational needs.
  • Build and maintain collaborative relationships with families, natural supports, community partners, and the multidisciplinary care team to promote positive outcomes for youth.

Qualifications

Education

  • Degree or Diploma in Child and Youth Care (CYC), Social Work, Human Services, or related field.

Certification

  • Standard First Aid and CPR.
  • Suicide Intervention
  • Valid Class 5 Driver’s License and vehicle
  • Proof of vehicle insurance (min. $2 million liability), registration and 3-year drivers abstract.
  • Indigenous Awareness
  • Medication Administration
  • De-Escalation
  • Trauma Informed Care
  • Harm Reduction
  • Food Safety
  • WHMIS

Experience

  • 3+ years’ experience supporting marginalized youth and vulnerable populations
  • 1+ years of leadership or supervisory experience, including employee supervision, coaching, training, and quality improvement initiatives.
  • Knowledge and experience in harm reduction, trauma-informed, resiliency, and solution-focused practices.
  • Strong crisis intervention and de-escalation skills, capable of remaining calm in high-pressure situations.
  • Experience supporting youth facing complex barriers, including mental health, substance use, poverty, trauma, LGBTQ2S+ identities, and newcomer/refugee experiences
  • Proficient in MS Office and database applications.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Competitive Salary: $54,080.00
  • 4 weeks vacation + 10 paid sick days
  • Robust Benefits Package
  • Employee Family Assistance Program (EFAP)
  • Health Spending Account (HSA)
  • RRSP Matching
  • Professional Development Opportunities

title: Specialty Artist - MAC
description:
OVERVIEW

Experience a place of energy, passion, and excitement. A place where the joy of discovery and uncommon artistry blend to create exhilarating buying experiences—for true beauty enthusiasts. At Ulta Beauty, we’re transforming the world one shade, one lash, one cut at a time. Because beauty is powerful.

If you seek greater purpose—a place of vision, mission, and lived values—where voices are heard, contributions valued and recognized and growth opportunities abound, consider Ulta Beauty. Nowhere else are the possibilities quite this beautiful.

GENERAL SUMMARY & SCOPE

The Specialty Artist – MAC is responsible for maximizing sales in the MAC brand (including color cosmetics, skincare, and fragrance) by engaging guests to determine their individual needs, assisting guests in the selection and purchase of merchandise, and maintaining overall store standards, including cleanliness and replenishment. They represent the image, products, and culture of Ulta Beauty and the MAC brand to the Ulta Beauty guest and support the Experience Manager (EM) through a focus on performance (service/retail sales and in-store events), people (guest service and associate culture), and process (operating procedures and compliance standards). This position requires professional caliber makeup artistry skills, exceptional guest service, and the aptitude to learn and communicate product knowledge.

PRINCIPAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES (*Essential Job Functions)

The Specialty Artist – MAC is a champion of Ulta Beauty’s mission, vision and values, and should demonstrate them skillfully and consistently by performing the following duties and responsibilities of the position (as well as all other projects/duties as assigned):

Performance

  • Meet or exceed MAC brand sales and service goals and contribute to meeting or exceeding the store’s goals related to retail and service sales, guest loyalty (including credit), omni-channel, and retail shrink as set by Ulta Beauty.
  • Build and maintain strong customer relationships by interfacing with existing guest base, maintaining active contact with a growing preferred guest list, and following up on guest inquiries.
  • Ensure that each guest receives exceptional service by greeting and engaging every guest, personalizing service to their needs, offering samples, and recommending complementary products and/or services.
  • Conduct personalized, professional caliber makeup demonstrations, applications, and lessons; skincare analyses; and product demonstrations with guests to MAC and Ulta Beauty brand standards.
  • Study and practice the Skill Certification requirements and complete as many skill sets as appropriate, within the specified time frame as set by Ulta Beauty and MAC brand.
  • Remain informed, participate in, and inform guests about promotions and marketing initiatives within the brand and throughout all categories/departments of the Ulta Beauty store.
  • Book appointments for and support the execution of services and in-store events that deliver an unrivaled guest experience while delivering on sales goals for the MAC brand and the store.
  • Take the initiative to stay informed regarding new and existing industry trends, products, and services during work time, and be knowledgeable about the ingredients and benefits of these trends, products, and services to better serve guests.
  • Maintain prompt, regular attendance.

People

  • Contribute to an inclusive environment that supports teammates, peers, and the internal and external guests served.
  • Share the benefits of the guest loyalty program, including credit and the Ulta Beauty app, with guests on the salesfloor.
  • Maintain and update an active clientele portfolio for MAC brand sales.
  • Serve as an Ulta Beauty and MAC brand ambassador with all store associates, brand partners, and guests by sharing product knowledge, makeup application techniques, information on makeup trends, and MAC consciousness programs and philosophies, including the “Back to MAC” program.
  • Maintain strong relationships with MAC brand partners through participation in required trainings and the execution of in-store events and promotions.
  • Regularly participate in ongoing training, including brand and category education, to enable continuous professional development and drive MAC brand sales performance.
  • Collaborate with managers and associates throughout the store to help grow the business.

Process

  • Be knowledgeable of and ensure adherence to Ulta Beauty’s policies, procedures, and standards.
  • Adhere to the Ulta Beauty and MAC brand dress code, including wearing brand assets as directed.
  • Drive sales by keeping assigned work area replenished, signed, and faced and ensuring testers are available and maintained in compliance with hygiene standards.
  • Maintain outstanding store and MAC operational standards, including participation in MAC recycling program and maintaining cleanliness of the MAC brand area and any additional assigned area, including the salesfloor, restrooms, cashwrap, backroom, and break area.
  • Participate in completing merchandise resets, planograms, marketing displays, physical inventory procedures, and processing shipment using Ulta Beauty and MAC brand provided technology and best practices.
  • Protect company assets by following loss prevention best practices and providing exceptional guest service.
  • Execute other operational tasks as directed.

JOB QUALIFICATIONS

Education

  • High school diploma is preferred
  • Cosmetology or demonstrator license where required by state law

Experience

  • Cosmetics artistry experience preferred

Skills

  • Demonstrates significant competency in sales, products, and service.
  • Ability to build and maintain strong customer relationships
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team
  • Ability to positively and proactively handle guest concerns and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment
  • Strong verbal communication and interpersonal skills

SPECIAL POSITION REQUIREMENTS

  • Work a flexible schedule to include days, evenings, weekends, and holidays
  • Attend brand sponsored trainings

WORKING CONDITIONS

  • Frequent mobility during shift
  • Frequent standing, bending, reaching, pulling, pushing, and twisting during shift
  • Continuous lifting and/or moving up to 10 lbs. during shift
  • Continuous coordination and manipulation of objects during shift

If an associate has a disability that prevents them from performing an essential function of the job, the Company will engage in the interactive process with the associate to determine whether there is a reasonable accommodation that will enable the associate to perform the essential functions of the job.




The pay range for this position is $20.00 - $30.00 / Hour. Exact pay will be based on factors including, but not limited to relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, level, shift, geographic location, and business and organizational needs. Eligible associates may also earn overtime pay as required by applicable law. Full-time positions are eligible for paid time off, health, dental, vision, life, and disability benefits. Part-time positions are eligible for dental, vision, life, and disability benefits. For additional information concerning our benefits, visit our Benefits and Career Development page: https://learn.bswift.com/ulta

ABOUT

At Ulta Beauty (NASDAQ: ULTA), the possibilities are beautiful. Ulta Beauty is the largest North American beauty retailer and the premier beauty destination for cosmetics, fragrance, skin care products, hair care products and salon services. We bring possibilities to life through the power of beauty each and every day in our stores and online with more than 25,000 products from approximately 500 well-established and emerging beauty brands across all categories and price points, including Ulta Beauty’s own private label. Ulta Beauty also offers a full-service salon in every store featuring—hair, skin, brow, and make-up services.

We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest records, conviction records, or other criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of any applicable state and local laws, including the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, and the New York City Fair Chance Act.

title: Engineer - NPI & Engineering (ECN & Component Obsolescence Management)
description:
Job Description

Engineer – ECN & Component Obsolescence Management

Position Title

Engineer / Senior Engineer – ECN & Alternate Parts Management

Department

NPI & Product Engineering / Sustenance Engineering

Reporting To

Manager – NPI & Product Engineering


Job Summary

Responsible for managing Engineering Change Notices (ECNs), Product Change Notifications (PCNs), component obsolescence activities, and alternate component qualification to ensure uninterrupted production and product lifecycle support. The role works closely with Design Engineering, SCM, Quality, Manufacturing, and Customers to identify risks from obsolete components and implement qualified alternate solutions with minimal business impact.


Key Responsibilities

Engineering Change Management (ECN/ECO)

  • Review and process Engineering Change Requests (ECRs), ECOs, and ECNs.
  • Evaluate the impact of engineering changes on:
    • BOM
    • Drawings
    • Specifications
    • Manufacturing processes
    • Inventory
  • Coordinate approvals from Engineering, Quality, Operations, and Supply Chain.
  • Track ECN implementation status and ensure timely closure.
  • Maintain revision control and documentation compliance within PLM/ERP systems.
  • Support NPI-to-production transitions through controlled implementation of engineering changes.

Component Obsolescence Management

  • Monitor component lifecycle status using OEM notifications, PCNs, and lifecycle databases.
  • Identify End-of-Life (EOL), Not Recommended for New Design (NRND), and obsolete components.
  • Assess the impact of obsolete parts on active products and customer programs.
  • Develop mitigation plans to address supply continuity risks.
  • Maintain an obsolescence risk register and provide periodic management reports.

Alternate Part Identification & Qualification

  • Identify suitable alternate components considering:
    • Form
    • Fit
    • Function
    • Reliability
    • Compliance requirements
  • Perform parametric comparison of alternate parts.
  • Coordinate qualification testing and validation activities.
  • Prepare technical justification reports and deviation requests.
  • Support AVL (Approved Vendor List) expansion activities.
  • Work with suppliers and manufacturers to evaluate alternative sourcing options.

BOM & Documentation Management

  • Update BOMs based on approved engineering changes.
  • Ensure all alternate parts are documented and approved before release.
  • Conduct BOM health checks and lifecycle analysis.
  • Maintain engineering databases and change records.

Cross Functional Coordination

  • Collaborate with:
    • Design Engineering
    • Procurement
    • Manufacturing Engineering
    • Quality Assurance
