title: Head of New Ventures
description:
JOB SUMMARY

The Head of New Ventures and Innovation is accountable for discovering where Vanguard Charitable’s future growth will come from, proving whether it is real, and building the path to scale. Through deep understanding of donor, advisor, nonprofit, and partner needs, evolving consumer behaviors, industry shifts, emerging technologies, and developments in adjacent markets, this leader identifies opportunities capable of producing outsized sustainable revenue and mission impact. The role translates insight into a portfolio of new ventures and operates the disciplined experimentation engine used to shape, test, fund, advance, pivot, transfer, or stop them. The position combines bold, original thinking with sound judgment about financial, regulatory, operational, technology, brand, and reputational constraints; manages an initial innovation investment pool; and develops rigorous business cases for additional funding when evidence supports incubation, transition, or scale.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

  • Build an ongoing discovery capability that identifies unmet and emerging needs among donors, advisors, nonprofits, and partners. Use direct client engagement, qualitative and quantitative research, behavioral observation, market data, and internal insight to understand changing expectations, friction points, motivations, and jobs to be done. (15%)
  • Scan philanthropy, wealth management, financial services, fintech, technology, consumer markets, and adjacent industries for shifts, disruptions, emerging business models, and transferable ideas. Connect weak signals and seemingly unrelated developments to define strategic opportunity spaces and generate differentiated growth theses for Vanguard Charitable. (10%)
  • Build and operate the enterprise experimentation engine, including clear intake, problem framing, hypothesis design, evidence standards, stage gates, decision rights, learning documentation, and pathways to advance, pivot, pause, transfer, or stop work. Create a repeatable system that increases the quality and pace of learning without lowering risk or control standards. (20%)
  • Develop and actively manage a portfolio of growth hypotheses spanning new revenue pools, clients, business models, products, services, partnerships, channels, and capabilities. Translate external insight into compelling concepts, maintain a balanced portfolio, and make disciplined prioritization and go/no-go decisions. (15%)
  • Design and lead hypothesis-specific experiments, prototypes, and pilots using fit-for-purpose resource models. Assemble small cross-functional teams and selectively use internal talent, contractors, consultants, vendors, strategic partners, research panels, accelerators, or other external capacity to test the highest-risk assumptions quickly and credibly. (15%)
  • Manage a growth portfolio with transparency and discipline. Set discovery and test budgets, track spend and learning against milestones, reallocate funds as evidence changes, and build compelling business cases for additional investment that address client value, revenue potential, economics, strategic fit, risk, operating requirements, and the next evidence needed. (10%)
  • Incubate validated concepts and create the path to launch or scale. Define the initial offer, experience, business and operating model, capability requirements, implementation sequence, ownership, and funding plan; partner with business leaders and enabling functions to transition ventures responsibly, and close unsuccessful concepts cleanly while retaining their learning. (5%)
  • Serve as a member of the leadership team; help to shape enterprise priorities and talent needs; communicate market insights, portfolio health, decisions, and strategic implications to executive and governance audiences; influence across enabling and business functions; and strengthen a culture of curiosity, imagination, candor, and evidence-based risk-taking. (10%)


QUALIFICATIONS

Education & Training

  • Bachelor’s degree required (Business, Economics, Public Policy, Data Science, or related field preferred)
  • Advanced degree or formal training in innovation, venture building, product discovery, design, experimentation, or entrepreneurship preferred, not required.

Licensure & Certification

  • None required.

Knowledge, Skill, and Ability

  • Knowledge of customer discovery, jobs-to-be-done, behavioral research, qualitative and quantitative insight methods, business model innovation, product or service incubation, lean experimentation, and portfolio management methods.
  • Knowledge of the forces shaping philanthropy, wealth management, financial services, technology, and consumer expectations, and able to identify relevant signals from adjacent sectors.
  • Knowledge of financial drivers and able to build revenue models, test economics, investment cases, scenario analyses, and funding recommendations appropriate to early-stage uncertainty.
  • Skilled in synthesizing client needs, behavioral observations, market intelligence, industry trends, and emerging technologies into distinct opportunity spaces and new growth concepts.
  • Skilled in connecting insights across seemingly unrelated markets or disciplines and applying them to create differentiated products, services, partnerships, channels, or business models.
  • Skilled in turning ambiguous opportunities into explicit hypotheses, testable assumptions, learning plans, measures, and clear decisions.
  • Skilled in designing low-cost, high-learning experiments and interpreting qualitative and quantitative evidence without overstating certainty.
  • Skilled in managing an innovation portfolio and budget, including sequencing bets, setting stage gates, reallocating resources, and stopping work when evidence does not support further investment.
  • Able to select and direct varied resource models, including cross-functional internal teams, fractional expertise, contractors, consultants, vendors, strategic partners, and external collaborators.
  • Able to generate original possibilities while working credibly within legal, compliance, financial, technology, operational, brand, and reputational constraints.
  • Skilled in executive communication and influence, including concise market perspectives, portfolio updates, business cases, recommendations, and candid articulation of what has been learned and what remains uncertain.
  • Able to lead through influence across functions, attract contributors to ambiguous work, build psychological safety for testing, and maintain accountability for decisions and outcomes.
  • Able to travel as business needs require.

Experience

  • Minimum of ten years of experience in innovation, new ventures, product or offer development, business strategy, entrepreneurship, growth, or a related discipline, including at least five years of leadership experience required.
  • Demonstrated experience uncovering unmet client or market needs and translating insight into new concepts, offers, ventures, or business models required.
  • Demonstrated experience building or materially improving an experimentation, incubation, venture, or innovation portfolio capability required.
  • Demonstrated experience taking new concepts from opportunity identification through testing and an evidence-based decision to stop, transition, launch, or scale required.
  • Experience managing investment budgets and securing incremental funding through business cases or governance decisions required.
  • Experience in financial services, fintech, philanthropy, nonprofit services, wealth management, or another regulated or trust-based environment preferred.

title: Security Architect
description:
Intelance is appointing a Security Architect as a contract associate for the definition phase of a major UK enterprise technology programme. You will provide a focused security review of the proposed integration approach and work with Intelance's Chief Enterprise Architect, Lead Integration Architect and Oracle Technical Architect. The work will set the security requirements for how systems, APIs, files, identities and sensitive data connect. The expected commitment is about 5 days across an 8 to 10 week period. Delivery will be mainly remote, with limited planned travel where needed.

Tasks

  • Review the current security controls affecting integrations, Oracle, bespoke applications and external connections.
  • Define security requirements for APIs, messaging, file transfer and service accounts.
  • Set identity, access, authentication, authorisation and privileged access requirements.
  • Define encryption, key and secret management requirements.
  • Define logging, monitoring, alerting and audit requirements.
  • Review network boundaries and data flows for security risks.
  • Identify the controls required before a connection can go live.
  • Provide security questions and scoring criteria for platform and supplier selection.
  • Rank security risks and recommend practical treatment.
  • Produce a concise security architecture review and requirements set.

Requirements

  • At least 8 years of security architecture experience.
  • Strong recent experience designing security for APIs and enterprise integrations.
  • Strong knowledge of identity and access, service accounts, secrets, encryption, API gateways, network separation, logging and monitoring.
  • Experience working across legacy systems and modern integration platforms.
  • Able to run threat modelling and turn risks into clear technical requirements.
  • Able to explain security decisions clearly to non technical leaders.
  • Clear written and spoken English.
  • Based in the United Kingdom, with the right to work in the United Kingdom.
  • Available for about 5 days across an 8 to 10 week period.

Experience with Oracle or ERP estates is useful. Experience in manufacturing, distribution or supply chain businesses is also useful. Experience with NCSC guidance or ISO 27001 environments is useful.

Benefits

  • £500 to £675 per day, depending on directly relevant experience.
  • Flexible delivery pattern across the agreed 8 to 10 week period.
  • Direct access to Intelance's Chief Enterprise Architect and senior client technology leaders.
  • A focused piece of work with named outputs and decision points.
  • Potential follow on security assurance work, subject to programme approval and performance.
  • Pre agreed travel expenses paid separately.

Please apply with a current CV. The process is a short screening form, a 30 minute introductory call and one focused technical discussion. We will move quickly and keep the process clear. The engagement will be subject to contract, reference checks and an IR35 status assessment.

PRINCIPAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES (*Essential Job Functions)

The Specialty Artist – MAC is a champion of Ulta Beauty’s mission, vision and values, and should demonstrate them skillfully and consistently by performing the following duties and responsibilities of the position (as well as all other projects/duties as assigned):

Performance

  • Meet or exceed MAC brand sales and service goals and contribute to meeting or exceeding the store’s goals related to retail and service sales, guest loyalty (including credit), omni-channel, and retail shrink as set by Ulta Beauty.
  • Build and maintain strong customer relationships by interfacing with existing guest base, maintaining active contact with a growing preferred guest list, and following up on guest inquiries.
  • Ensure that each guest receives exceptional service by greeting and engaging every guest, personalizing service to their needs, offering samples, and recommending complementary products and/or services.
  • Conduct personalized, professional caliber makeup demonstrations, applications, and lessons; skincare analyses; and product demonstrations with guests to MAC and Ulta Beauty brand standards.
  • Study and practice the Skill Certification requirements and complete as many skill sets as appropriate, within the specified time frame as set by Ulta Beauty and MAC brand.
  • Remain informed, participate in, and inform guests about promotions and marketing initiatives within the brand and throughout all categories/departments of the Ulta Beauty store.
  • Book appointments for and support the execution of services and in-store events that deliver an unrivaled guest experience while delivering on sales goals for the MAC brand and the store.
  • Take the initiative to stay informed regarding new and existing industry trends, products, and services during work time, and be knowledgeable about the ingredients and benefits of these trends, products, and services to better serve guests.

Why Join Lynd?

title: Director Jobsite Communications
description:
Build the Future with Us — EquipmentShare is Hiring a Director Jobsite Communications

At EquipmentShare, we’re not just filling a role — we’re assembling the best team on the planet to build something that’s never been built before. We’re on a mission to transform an industry that’s been stuck in the past by empowering contractors and communities through innovative technology, real-time support, and a team that truly cares.

We’re hiring a Director Jobsite Communications who will lead the growth and operations of our radio rental business. Our radio portfolio includes standard two-way radios, intrinsically safe radios, digital radios, Motorola R7 radios, repeaters, antennas, chargers, speakers/microphones, and related communication equipment. This role is responsible for driving operational excellence, customer satisfaction, and profitable growth across our telecommunications offering. The Director will own the end-to-end telecommunications rental operation - from determining the right equipment and fleet strategy, to ensuring radios are configured, maintained, deployed, returned, and ready for the next customer. This leader will also work closely with Sales, Operations, Technology, Service, and field teams to make radio rentals a scalable and profitable part of the EquipmentShare business.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute the strategy for growing EquipmentShare's telecommunications rental offering.
  • Partner with Sales to educate teams on the radio portfolio, use cases, capabilities, and limitations, and develop compelling rental solutions tailored to construction, industrial, utility, event, and other customer needs.
  • Manage, coach, and develop a small team of telecommunications professionals.

Fleet Lifecycle

  • Establish the right mix of radios, accessories, and communication solutions for different customer and jobsite requirements.
  • Develop and own the end-to-end radio fleet strategy and lifecycle, including purchasing, replacement, acquisition, deployment, maintenance, refurbishment, and retirement, based on utilization, demand, profitability, technology, and total cost of ownership.
  • Monitor fleet utilization and identify opportunities to improve asset productivity.
  • Develop and manage processes for tracking, preventing, and recovering lost or damaged radio equipment, ensuring timely resolution and minimizing financial impact.

Operations and Process

  • Create scalable operating procedures for quoting, provisioning, programming, deployment, returns, inspection, repair, and redeployment.
  • Establish standards for radio configuration, programming, labeling, inventory control, and readiness.
  • Establish service-level expectations and performance metrics for the radio business.

Technical and Vendor

  • Maintain deep working knowledge of two-way radio technology, including digital radio systems, repeaters, antennas, accessories, and intrinsically safe equipment.
  • Maintain current knowledge of and ensure compliance with all applicable FCC requirements and telecommunications regulations.
  • Partner with vendors and manufacturers to manage product relationships.
  • Work with internal technology teams to integrate telecommunications capabilities with EquipmentShare's broader T3 platform and connected-jobsite strategy.

Commercial and Reporting

  • Own and report on key business metrics including revenue, gross margin, utilization, fleet productivity, repair costs, loss rates, and customer satisfaction.
  • Provide regular business updates and recommendations to senior leadership.

Why EquipmentShare?

Because we do things differently — and we think you’ll feel it from day one. We’re a people-first company powered by cutting-edge technology. That means our proprietary T3 platform doesn’t just run our business — it also makes your job easier, safer, and more connected. Whether you’re behind the wheel, under the hood, leading a branch, or closing deals — tech supports you, and you drive us forward.

We’re a team of problem-solvers, go-getters, and builders. And we’re looking for teammates who take pride in doing meaningful work and want to be part of building something special.

Perks & Benefits

  • Monthly Family Dinner Night — We treat you and your family to dinner every month, because family comes first. (An employee favorite!) *restrictions apply
  • Competitive compensation
  • Full medical, dental, and vision coverage for full-time employees
  • Generous PTO + paid holidays
  • 401(k) + company match
  • Tool and boot reimbursements (role dependent)
  • Gym membership stipend + wellness programs (earn PTO and prizes!)
  • Company events, food truck nights, and monthly team dinners
  • 16 hours of paid volunteer time per year — give back to the community you call home
  • Career advancement, leadership training, and professional development opportunities
  • Access to industry leading diagnostic tools

About You

You want to be part of a team that’s not just changing an industry for the sake of change — we’re transforming it to make it safer, more secure, and more productive. You bring grit, heart, and humility to your work, and you’re excited about the opportunity to grow within a fast-paced, mission-driven environment.

We’re looking for people who:

  • See challenges as opportunities
  • Embrace change and continuous improvement
  • Bring energy, effort, and optimism every day

Skills & Qualifications

  • Experience managing repeater systems and jobsite communication infrastructure.
  • Experience with radio programming, configuration, fleet management, or telecommunications operations.
  • Experience supporting construction, industrial, utility, energy, or large-scale jobsite operations.
  • Experience working with vendors, manufacturers, distributors, or technology partners, preferred
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to make decisions in a fast-moving environment
  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills.
  • Comfortable operating hands-on when necessary while also developing scalable processes and strategy.
  • Entrepreneurial mindset with a high degree of ownership and accountability.

Required Skills/Abilities:

  • Strong technical understanding of commercial two-way radio systems and related equipment, including Motorola Solutions products
  • Experience managing repeater systems and jobsite communication infrastructure.
  • Experience with radio programming, configuration, fleet management, or telecommunications operations.
  • Experience supporting construction, industrial, utility, energy, or large-scale jobsite operations.
  • Experience working with vendors, manufacturers, distributors, or technology partners, preferred
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to make decisions in a fast-moving environment
  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills.
  • Comfortable operating hands-on when necessary while also developing scalable processes and strategy.
  • Entrepreneurial mindset with a high degree of ownership and accountability.

Education and Experience:

  • At least 7 years of experience in telecommunications, two-way radio, field communications, or a closely related industry.
  • At least 3 years of leadership or people-management experience.Experience building a new business line or scaling a rapidly growing operation.
  • Familiarity with GPS, Wi-Fi, cellular, or other jobsite connectivity technologies.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage business performance, budgets, and operational metrics.

Physical Requirements:

  • Ability to travel nationwide up to 50% of the time.
  • Must be able to sit for prolonged periods at a desk and work on a computer.
  • Must be able to stand, bend, walk, and stoop for extended periods

A Workplace For All

At EquipmentShare, we believe the best solutions come from a team that reflects the world around us. Our initiative — A Workplace For All — is rooted in the belief that we must work together to solve some of the toughest problems in construction. That means attracting, developing, and retaining great people from all walks of life.

We value different backgrounds, talents, and perspectives. We want you to feel like you belong here — because you do.

EquipmentShare is an EOE M/F/D/V.

Employment is contingent on passing a background check. Additionally, some roles require passing a drug test, depending on the job responsibilities.

title: Coordonnateur, environnement, santé et sécurité (EHS Coordinator)
description:
À titre de coordonnateur ou coordonnatrice en environnement, santé et sécurité (ESS), vous contribuerez activement à la conformité réglementaire, à la performance environnementale et à la sécurité du site en assurant le suivi des systèmes ESS, des audits et des rapports. Grâce à votre expertise, vous soutiendrez la gestion des risques, l’amélioration continue et les initiatives de développement durable en collaboration avec les équipes internes et les partenaires externes.

Dans ce rôle, vous exercerez une influence directe sur des résultats qui comptent, dans un environnement dynamique et collaboratif offrant de réelles possibilités de développement au sein d’une structure d’entreprise bien établie.

  • Assurer le leadership des systèmes SSE (EHS) (PSM, EMS, SMSR, STW) et soutenir une culture de conformité et d’amélioration continue
  • Piloter les audits (internes, permis de travail, documentaires) et coordonner les exigences légales et corporatives
  • Produire et analyser les rapports réglementaires et corporatifs (INRP, émissions, eau, énergie, LCPE, durabilité, etc.)
  • Gérer et optimiser les données environnementales via Métrio et autres outils analytiques
  • Participer activement aux analyses de risques (PHA) et mener des analyses de causes racines à fort impact
  • Déployer et maintenir des programmes robustes de permis de travail et de gestion des contracteurs
  • Planifier et réaliser des exercices d’urgence et assurer la mise à jour des plans associés
  • Contribuer aux initiatives stratégiques en durabilité et aux programmes corporatifs
  • Collaborer avec des équipes multidisciplinaires et des partenaires externes pour atteindre les objectifs SSE
Qualifications
  • Baccalauréat ou maîtrise en santé et sécurité du travail (SST), de préférence
  • Un certificat universitaire en SST est requis pour les personnes candidates qui ne détiennent pas de baccalauréat ou de maîtrise dans un domaine connexe
  • 3-5 ans d’expérience dans un poste similaire
  • Expérience dans des industries à haut risque (fabrication, produits chimiques, énergie, environnement)
  • Une expérience en milieu syndiqué constitue un atout
  • Solide connaissance de la législation québécoise en matière de santé et de sécurité du travail (SST)
  • Solide compréhension des exigences réglementaires et des systèmes de gestion ESS (ISO 14001)
  • Solides compétences en audit, en analyse de données et en amélioration continue
  • Esprit analytique et capacité à résoudre des problèmes complexes
  • Solides aptitudes interpersonnelles et capacité à exercer une influence auprès des autres
  • Capacité à travailler de façon autonome, avec un grand souci du détail
  • Langues — Bilinguisme requis (français et anglais); la maîtrise de l’anglais est requise pour ce poste, en plus du français, puisque cette fonction exige des communications directes et régulières avec nos sites de fabrication aux États-Unis et ailleurs dans le monde
________________________________________________________________

As an EHS Coordinator, you will actively contribute to regulatory compliance, environmental performance, and site safety by monitoring EHS systems, audits, and reporting. With your expertise, you will support risk management, continuous improvement, and sustainability initiatives in collaboration with internal teams and external partners.

In this role, you'll have direct influence over outcomes that matter and you'll do it in a dynamic, collaborative environment with genuine development opportunities within a structured corporate setting.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead EHS systems (PSM, EMS, SMSR, STW) and foster a culture of compliance and continuous improvement
  • Lead internal, work permit, and documentation audits and coordinate legal and corporate requirements
  • Prepare and analyze regulatory and corporate reports (INRP, emissions, water, energy, LCPE, sustainability, etc.)

  • Actively participate in risk analyses (PHA) and conduct high-impact root cause analyses
  • Implement and maintain robust/effective work permit
  • Plan and conduct emergency drills and ensure related emergency plans are kept up to date
  • Contribute to strategic sustainability initiatives and corporate programs
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams and external partners to achieve EHS objectives

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Occupational Health & Safety (OHS/SST) preferred
  • A university certificate in OHS/SST is required for candidates who do not hold a bachelor’s or master’s degree in a related field
  • 3 to 5 years' experience in a similar position
  • Experience in high-risk industries (manufacturing, chemical, energy, environment)
  • Experience in a unionized environment is a plus
  • Strong knowledge of Quebec occupational health and safety legislation (SST/OHS)
  • Strong understanding of regulatory requirements and EHS management systems (ISO14001)
  • Strong skills in audit, data analysis, and continuous improvement
  • Analytical mindset and ability to solve complex problems
  • Strong interpersonal skills and ability to influence others
  • Ability to work independently, with strong attention to detail
  • Language - Bilingual required (French/English); Fluency in English is required for this role, in addition to French, as this position involves regular direct communication with our U.S. and global manufacturing sites

Weekend Sign Installer

Are you looking for a flexible way to earn extra income on the weekends—and potentially grow it into your own small business? This position is a remote opportunity. Applicant should live in or near the zip-code listed
Earn $70–$125 per weekend to start, with the opportunity to grow to $250–$350+ per weekend as you take on additional routes. Our Average Installer makes approximately $300 per weekend.
Weekend Directional Service is seeking reliable independent contractors to place and pick up temporary directional signs. This is a simple, independent role that can be completed in just a few hours each weekend.

What You’ll Do
  • Place signs between Friday 5:00 PM – Saturday 10:00 AM
  • Pick up signs between Sunday 6:00 PM – Monday 8:00 AM
  • Follow provided Google Maps routes and/or placement lists
  • Complete routes in any order within the allowed time windows
  • Store signs safely between weekends
  • Use your own vehicle to complete local routes
Most routes consist of 30–60 signs and typically take 45 minutes to 1.5 hours once you’re familiar with the area.
Why This Opportunity Works
  • Flexible schedule that fits around other commitments
  • Consistent weekend work available
  • Independent, low-stress work environment
  • Opportunity to grow earnings by taking on more routes
This role is ideal for rideshare drivers, delivery drivers, students, retirees, veterans, or anyone looking for reliable supplemental income.
Pay & Perks
  • $70–$125 per weekend to start
  • Opportunity to earn $200–$300+ per weekend as you grow
  • Signing Bonus
  • Direct deposit, paid bi-weekly
  • Training provided (video + support from managers)

Requirements
  • Valid driver’s license
  • Current auto insurance
  • Reliable vehicle with space for 30–60 signs
  • Smartphone (iPhone or Android, ~4 years old or newer)
  • Ability to lift and place signs outdoors in various weather conditions
  • Ability to hammer stakes 6–8 inches into the ground as needed

title: Director of Development
description:
Help expand the philanthropic support behind Harbor Homes’ housing, shelter, and supportive services.

The Role:


Harbor Homes of Martha’s Vineyard is seeking a strategic, relationship-driven Director of Development to lead and grow the organization’s fundraising program during an important period of expansion.


Harbor Homes works to ensure that everyone on Martha’s Vineyard has access to safe shelter, essential resources, and the support needed to build a thriving, self-sufficient life. We provide a continuum of housing, shelter, outreach, and supportive services for Islanders experiencing or at risk of homelessness.


Reporting to the Executive Director, the Director of Development will provide leadership for the annual fund, major gifts, foundation relations, and the Harbor Homes Center Capital Campaign while building the systems and relationships needed to sustain long-term philanthropic support.


This is an opportunity for an experienced fundraiser who enjoys cultivating meaningful relationships, improving fundraising systems, and turning strategy into action. As Harbor Homes’ dedicated fundraising professional, the Director of Development will help lead a transformational capital campaign and develop the fundraising capacity needed to expand housing, shelter, and supportive services across the Island.


The Director of Development will work closely with the Executive Director, Board of Directors, staff, campaign volunteers, and fundraising consultants to achieve goals that directly support Harbor Homes’ mission and future growth.


Why Join Harbor Homes?


Eligible full-time employees receive:

  • A retirement plan with an employer match of up to 4%.
  • An employer-funded Health Reimbursement Arrangement providing up to $4,000 annually for eligible healthcare expenses.
  • Three weeks of paid vacation to start.
  • 40 hours of paid sick time annually.
  • The opportunity to take on a significant leadership role in a growing, community-based organization addressing one of Martha’s Vineyard’s most pressing challenges.


Benefits are subject to eligibility requirements and the terms of the applicable plans and policies.


What You’ll Do:


The Director of Development will:

  • Lead Harbor Homes’ comprehensive annual fundraising program and develop annual fundraising plans, calendars, goals, and strategies.
  • Build and manage relationships with current and prospective donors, including leadership and major-gift prospects, through identification, cultivation, solicitation, recognition, and stewardship.
  • Serve as the day-to-day manager of the Harbor Homes Center Capital Campaign.
  • Coordinate campaign planning, prospect strategy, volunteer support, donor tracking, and reporting.
  • Manage foundation relationships, identify new funding opportunities, and prepare competitive grant proposals and reports.
  • Partner with the Executive Director, Board members, staff, volunteers, and consultants on fundraising strategy and execution.
  • Develop compelling fundraising messages, case statements, appeals, and donor communications.
  • Monitor fundraising performance and use data to guide strategy.
  • Build and improve the systems needed to support Harbor Homes’ long-term fundraising capacity.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned.


Want to learn more about the position? [View the complete Director of Development job description.]


What You Bring:


The ideal candidate is a confident relationship builder who is comfortable with both strategic planning and hands-on execution. This person can move naturally between meeting with a major donor, preparing a grant proposal, analyzing fundraising results, and preparing a Board member or volunteer for a donor conversation.


Ideal candidates will bring:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.
  • At least five years of progressively responsible experience in fundraising, business development, sales, philanthropy, or a related field.
  • Demonstrated success securing significant philanthropic investments, sponsorships, or major client relationships.
  • Experience managing multiple fundraising initiatives or revenue-generating projects.
  • Strong relationship-building and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Excellent writing, presentation, and proposal-development abilities.
  • Strong organizational, project-management, and analytical skills.
  • Experience using donor CRM systems and fundraising databases; familiarity with Bloomerang or a similar system is preferred.
  • An entrepreneurial, proactive, and adaptable approach.
  • The ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with donors, volunteers, Board members, colleagues, and community partners.
  • A genuine commitment to Harbor Homes’ mission and the people we serve.


We recognize that great candidates may not meet every qualification listed above. If you are excited about this opportunity and believe your experience aligns with the role, we encourage you to apply.


Position Details:

Position: Director of Development

Status: Full-time, Exempt

Reports to: Executive Director

Location: Martha’s Vineyard, Massachusetts

Organization: Harbor Homes of Martha’s Vineyard


The position is primarily office-based but includes donor meetings, community events, campaign activities, and occasional travel on or off Martha’s Vineyard. Occasional evening or weekend work may be required. Hybrid or remote work may be considered based on organizational needs and with the Executive Director’s approval.


To Apply

Please submit an application. Applications will be reviewed as received.


Questions?

title: Quality Lead, Agentic AI Workflow Evaluation
description:
Innodata (Nasdaq: INOD) is a global data engineering company. We believe that data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are inextricably linked. Our mission is to enable the responsible advancement of artificial intelligence by providing the data, evaluation frameworks, and human expertise required to build AI systems that can be trusted at scale. We provide a range of transferable solutions, platforms, and services for Generative AI / AI builders and adopters. In every relationship, we honor our 36+ year legacy delivering the highest quality data and outstanding outcomes for our customers.

Scope of the Role:

We are standing up a dedicated onsite team to evaluate complex, real-world agentic AI workflows for a frontier AI customer. Reviewers work through ambiguous, multi-step scenarios inside isolated test environments, assessing whether AI agents complete tasks safely, respect user intent and consent, and hold up under close scrutiny. The Quality Lead is the person accountable for whether that output is any good.

This is a senior individual contributor role. You will not manage the reviewers — that sits with the Engagement Manager — but you set the standard they are held to. You own the audit sample, run calibration, keep the rubric usable as real cases stress it, and train reviewers into the work. You are also the deputy: when the Engagement Manager is out, the engagement runs on you.

The quality approach here is not fully defined. We expect you to build it in partnership with the customer's quality leads, or at minimum to take what they have, run it honestly, and come back with specific recommendations for where it falls short.

What You’ll Own:

  • Own the quality system for the engagement: audit design, sampling strategy, scoring standards, and how quality gets measured and reported
  • Build that system with the customer's quality leads where none exists, and where one does, operate it and recommend concrete improvements based on what the data shows
  • Re-score a sample of reviewer output as a second pass; identify error patterns rather than isolated mistakes
  • Run calibration sessions: surface disagreement, work it to resolution, and document the reasoning so the outcome holds for future cases
  • Maintain rubric health — flag criteria that are ambiguous, overlapping, or silent on cases the team keeps hitting, and drive revisions through the customer
  • Train and onboard new reviewers, including nesting plans, ramp criteria, and the judgment call on when someone is production-ready
  • Give the Engagement Manager the evidence behind performance conversations: who is drifting, on what, and whether coaching is working
  • Report quality trends to the Engagement Manager and, alongside them, to the customer
  • Deputize for the Engagement Manager on delivery operations during absences
  • Maintain information security, privacy, and facility access practices required by the customer's onsite environment

You’ll Thrive in This Role If You Have:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience
  • 4+ years in quality assurance, quality management, or senior review work within annotation, evaluation, trust and safety, or a similarly judgment-intensive domain
  • Direct experience owning a quality function: you designed the audit, not just executed someone else’s
  • Significant experience with AI/ML evaluation work: annotation, red-teaming, RLHF, model or agent evaluation, or trust and safety review
  • Hands-on familiarity with agentic systems: tool use, multi-step task execution, sandboxed environments, and common failure modes
  • Demonstrated ability to run calibration with peers — including holding a position under disagreement and changing it when the argument is better
  • Strong written communication; able to document a scoring standard clearly enough that a reviewer can apply it and an auditor can check it
  • Comfortable in spreadsheets and in a dashboarding tool, with enough Python or SQL to pull and slice your own data (you will not be asked to build interfaces)
  • Experience training or onboarding reviewers into rubric-based work

The expected hourly salary range for this position is $75-85 p/hour, based on experience, skills, and qualifications.

CFD Research is looking for a Senior Computer Vision Engineer who will design, develop, and optimize advanced computer vision and multi‑sensor fusion algorithms supporting GEOINT‑mission workflows. The candidate will participate in the development of deep learning models, real‑time tracking systems, and GPU‑accelerated pipelines deployed in operational environments. You will shape next‑generation tools that integrate imaging physics, ML-based behavior inference, and multi‑sensor fusion. CFD Research values first-principles reasoning and physically interpretable models, so experience developing hybrid systems that combine calibrated sensor models, deterministic algorithms, probabilistic inference, and learned components is particularly desirable. Candidates should be motivated by building systems that are scientifically explainable, empirically validated, and capable of operating robustly across both synthetic and real-world sensing environments.

  • Develop and implement deep learning computer vision models, with a focus on sensor fusion and target tracking
  • Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to design, develop, test, and deploy technical solutions in Python or C++
  • Utilize GPU programming, including CUDA or RAPIDs, to optimize the performance of computer vision applications
  • Contribute to the architecture and implementation of novel single and multi-sensor detection and tracking and fusion of targets

Basic Qualifications:

  • 6+ years of experience developing computer vision algorithms for detection, tracking, or multi‑sensor fusion in remote sensing or GEOINT‑relevant environments
  • 2+ years of experience applying deep learning to computer vision problems using transformer‑based or self‑supervised architectures
  • Candidate must possess an ACTIVE TS/SCI security clearance to be considered.
  • Experience implementing model pipelines in Python or C++, including training, evaluation, and deployment workflows
  • Knowledge of GPU‑accelerated development using CUDA, RAPIDS, or other GPU programming frameworks

title: Executive Business Partner
description:
We're Jiffy! We launched over a decade ago with a simple mission: use technology to combine an unparalleled level of customer service with the fastest delivery in the blank apparel, direct-to-film transfer, and custom apparel industry. We're more than a T-Shirt company; we're a support system for the creator economy, the home hobbyist, the small business owner, and more. Today, we help millions of small businesses and customers build their vision from scratch! We are bootstrapped and founder-owned, no VC playbook and no burn-rate math, and we run at the forefront of applying AI to a real operating business.

As our Executive Business Partner, you'll run the Office of the President. This is an Executive Assistant role and a Business Operations role in one seat, working directly with our President & COO. Half the job is running the executive office at a world-class level: calendar, travel, meetings, follow-through. The other half is utility-player work across the functions that report to the President, operations, customer experience, finance, data, engineering, and scoped people-operations support run through Talent Acquisition and Finance. You'll get the President's time pointed at the right problems, own the follow-through ledger that holds the whole leadership cadence together, and take on real cross-functional work as the business needs it.

This is a rare, full-spectrum role, and it's built as a launchpad rather than a ceiling. You'll do all of it with AI as your default way of working, in an office where reporting, research, and triage are already largely produced by AI agents, and where your judgment is the reason that output can be trusted. It is the best seat in the company for learning how a large e-commerce operation actually runs. A candidate who wants a pure analyst seat, or who sees calendar and travel work as beneath them, is not what we are looking for.

You'll report directly to the President & COO and work daily with other sr. leaders, plus Finance, Engineering, Talent Acquisition, and CX leadership. You'll also carry a dotted line to our Sr. Director of Corporate Affairs, supporting her work including North America group events. We move fast and operate lean, so we need someone who automates instead of adding steps, checks their own numbers before anyone else has to, and tells us what's off plan before we ask. This role sits in Irvine, with occasional travel and some flexibility outside standard hours when the calendar demands it.

Executive Operations, End to End

  • Own the President's calendar, prioritization, conflict resolution, protecting focus time, and making every meeting earn its slot.
  • Own travel, expenses, and logistics, handled so well nobody thinks about them.
  • Hold the discretion the seat requires. Compensation, personnel, strategy, and off-boarding material crosses this desk every week and stops here.
  • Be the reliable front door to the Office of the President for the leadership team and for outside partners.

Meeting Excellence & Follow-Through

  • Agendas and pre-reads before, decisions and owners captured during, commitments chased to done after.
  • Own a follow-through ledger across every function — what was promised, by whom, by when, and whether it is actually happening.
  • Own the weekly exceptions list: the short set of things off plan, each with a named owner and a date.
  • Escalate early. A commitment quietly slipping is the thing this seat exists to catch.

An Office That Runs on AI

  • Work automation-first: draft, research, summarize, reconcile, and prepare with AI tools, then apply your own judgment before anything reaches the President or leaves the office.
  • Treat any task you do more than twice as a candidate for automation; build and maintain the workflows that produce recurring briefings, trackers, and reports.
  • Own the quality gate on machine-made output. Nothing ships until you have checked the numbers against their source in this seat, confidently wrong is worse than slow.
  • Handle the exceptions AI gets wrong, then fix the workflow so the same exception does not recur.
  • Leave the office more automated at the end of each quarter than it was at the start.

Cross-Functional Projects & Business Ownership

  • Pick up what the business needs next: a customer-experience audit, a finance process cleanup, a data pull behind a pricing decision, an operations scramble.
  • Direct operational support to Kevin of Exectuive GM, follow-through, and project support on the operations side, on a standing basis rather than ad hoc.
  • Dotted-line support to our Sr. Director of Corporate Affairs, including planning and execution support for North America group events.
  • Own one recurring business report end to end, its definition, its data source, and its accuracy.
  • Drive at least one cross-functional issue per quarter to a decision with named owners and dates, and present the outcome yourself.
  • Learn the business lines well enough to be useful in the room, not just to schedule it.

People & HR Support

This is defined, owned work with named partners not open-ended "help the HR team."

  • Onboarding coordination: run the pre-start checklist for new hires equipment, systems access, workspace, merch box, and first-week welcome logistics. Confirm access is provisioned and working on day one, not day three.
  • Off-boarding coordination: run the departure checklist with IT, Finance, and the manager. Confirm every system, credential, and building access is cut on the effective date. This is a same-day, verified-closed process, and it is one of the most sensitive things you'll own.
  • Candidate Scheduling, pipeline support and general admin tasks for the Senior Director of Talent Acquisition. This can include scheduling and coordination for interview loops, candidate communication, pipeline hygiene, and screening support on defined reqs. Scope is set by TA, and TA owns the decision.
  • Finance-adjacent people ops: support headcount tracking, offer paperwork routing, and new-hire cost setup as directed by Finance.

Requirements

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree required
  • 2–5 years of experience at a fast-moving company with an agile environment
  • Two or more years of experience supporting senior leaders, running an executive office, or managing cross-functional business projects.
  • A working portfolio of AI-built automations, at least two or three workflows you personally built and can walk through, with the measurable result: hours saved, errors avoided, or volume absorbed without added headcount.
  • Demonstrated judgment about where AI tools fail. You can point to a time a tool handed you a confident wrong answer, explain how you caught it, and describe the verification habit you kept afterward.
  • Hands-on data fluency in spreadsheets. Given a dataset and a question, you can produce the figure, cite where it came from, and name the conditions that would make it wrong.
  • Experience writing executive-level briefings, including at least one instance of delivering unwelcome news to a senior stakeholder in writing.
  • A serious appetite to learn e-commerce and operations from the ground up, and willingness to be measured against a defined learning bar at six and twelve months.
  • Able to work hybrid from our Irvine office approximately three days per week, with occasional travel and flexibility outside standard hours when the calendar requires it.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting a C-level executive or running an executive office at a fast-moving (start up) company.
  • Exposure to e-commerce, apparel, distribution, 3PL, or another high-volume, product-based operation.
  • Financial statement literacy — you can read a P&L and ask a useful question about it.
  • Hands-on with agent-building and automation tooling (Claude, Apps Script, Zapier / Make / n8n, or similar) and comfortable in spreadsheets at a level beyond pivot tables.
  • Experience at a bootstrapped, profitable, or otherwise resource-disciplined company where nobody was coming to do it for you.
  • Experience coordinating onboarding, offboarding, or recruiting logistics in a small, fast-moving people function.

title: Senior Staff Quantum Scientist
location: Albuquerque, New Mexico, United States; Boulder, Colorado, United States
description:
About IonQ:

IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance.

Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.

Role Overview

Role:

We are looking for a Senior Staff Quantum Scientist to join our Science team at IonQ. In this role, you will take a leading role in our research efforts, driving experimental efforts and the architecture of our future generation quantum systems.

We are pioneering advancements in quantum computing by utilising trapped ion technology and our proprietary laser-free quantum control methods. Our research and development efforts build on our fully integrated quantum processors that can be fabricated within standard silicon foundries. This unique approach allows us to leverage the highest-performing qubit technology while ensuring scalability and manufacturability using existing semiconductor fabrication technology.

We approach quantum computing with a focus on minimising errors, striving to achieve ultra-low gate errors at scale. Our immediate objective is to develop functional quantum computers within the NISQ regime, aiming to construct fault-tolerant machines that require minimal QEC overhead. Our recent breakthroughs include achieving 99.97% fidelity in two-qubit gates and 99.9992% fidelity in single-qubit operations without error correction, setting new industry standards for performance.

Responsibilities:

As a Senior Staff Quantum Scientist you will be at the forefront of our research and development, taking a leading role within our experimental science team. You will be responsible for driving innovation in coherent control, calibration, and benchmarking at scale, with a particular focus on enabling ultra-low error rates and system reliability across larger trapped-ion devices.

You will work hands-on with our current hardware, with work spanning design, debugging, and executing experiments, developing novel control schemes, and pushing the boundaries of system performance.

Beyond hands-on experiments, you will help shape technical direction, mentor junior scientists, and ensure our work translates into scalable, fault-tolerant systems.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Lead the prototyping and characterisation of advanced coherent control schemes for trapped-ion qubits using laser and microwave fields.
  • Drive system-level benchmarking and optimisation, ensuring near-term devices achieve world-leading performance and stability.
  • Validate and integrate new trap technologies (e.g. on-chip electronics or photonics) to support scaling towards error-corrected architectures.
  • Guide junior scientists in experimental design, analysis, and presentation of results.
  • Represent IonQ at conferences and external collaborations.

Requirements:

To be successful, you will need a strong foundation in atomic or qubit-related physics, developed through a PhD in physics or a closely related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and practical experience. We are looking for at least seven years of post-PhD experience in academia or industry, or equivalent relevant research experience, with the ability to lead projects, work autonomously and guide junior scientists.

Proven experience in quantum control, with hands-on work in calibration, benchmarking or coherent control of qubits, will be key to success. Practical skills in control software, hardware integration or experimental data analysis are also important.

You’d be a great fit with:

This work connects experimental physics with control hardware, software and data analysis. Experience linking these areas will help you investigate system performance and develop coherent control schemes for trapped-ion devices.

Technical leadership also means helping colleagues design experiments and communicate their results. Your experience of collaboration, mentoring and sharing scientific findings will support that part of the role.

  • Deep experience in AMO physics or quantum computing. Trapped-ion experience is useful but is not required.
  • Experience in spectroscopy or simulation of multilevel systems, control hardware characterisation, gate fidelity benchmarking or running algorithms on hardware.
  • Strong proficiency in programming and data analysis.
  • A track record of collaboration across teams and clear communication of complex scientific results through publications, talks or conferences.

The total compensation package includes base salary, bonus, equity, and a range of benefits available on our career site.

Compensation will vary based on individual factors such as education, qualifications, and experience of the final candidate(s), specific office location, and calibration against relevant market data and internal team equity. Posted base salary figures are subject to change as new market data becomes available. Our benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans, matching 401(k), unlimited PTO and paid holidays, parental/adoption leave, legal insurance, and a home technology stipend. Details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided when a candidate receives an offer of employment.

Established in Taiwan in 1974, Hon Hai Technology Group, commonly known as Foxconn, is the world’s largest electronics manufacturer and leading provider of technological solutions with a network of over 200 campuses across 24 countries. As of 2023, Foxconn ranks 32nd among the Fortune Global 500 and reported a revenue of approximately USD $213 billion in 2024.

The company’s diverse product offerings span four major segments: smart consumer electronics, cloud and networking solutions, computing and various other components. Foxconn makes 40% of the consumer electronics that we find in our everyday lives. In recent years, Hon Hai has adopted the 3+3 strategy, focusing on three emerging industries - electric vehicles, digital health solutions, and robotics - while leveraging three key technologies: next-generation communications, artificial intelligence (AI), and semiconductors. Hon Hai Technology Group is deeply committed to championing environmental sustainability within its manufacturing processes. title: AI Voice Evaluation Specialist
location: Remote - Alabama  ; Remote - Alaska  ; Remote - Arkansas  ; Remote - Delaware  ; Remote - Florida  ; Remote - Georgia  ; Remote - Indiana  ; Remote - Maryland  ; Remote - Massachusetts  ; Remote - New Hampshire  ; Remote - New Jersey  ; Remote - New York  ; Remote - South Carolina  ; Remote - Texas
description:
Innodata (Nasdaq: INOD) is a global data engineering company. We believe that data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are inextricably linked. Our mission is to enable the responsible advancement of artificial intelligence by providing the data, evaluation frameworks, and human expertise required to build AI systems that can be trusted at scale. We provide a range of transferable solutions, platforms, and services for Generative AI / AI builders and adopters. In every relationship, we honor our 36+ year legacy delivering the highest quality data and outstanding outcomes for our customers.

Scope of the Role:

We are looking for detail-oriented Voice Specialists to evaluate the performance of AI models through real-time, voice-based conversations. In this role, you will interact with two different AI models using the same assigned scenario, carefully compare their responses, and provide structured evaluations based on defined quality criteria.

The goal of the evaluation is to create a fair, consistent comparison between models and identify which model delivers the stronger overall conversational experience.

What You’ll Own:

  • Review an assigned scenario and roleplay a natural conversation with two different AI models.
  • Conduct comparable conversations with Model A and Model B, keeping the scenario, conversational approach, and overall interaction as consistent as possible.
  • Maintain approximately the same number of conversational turns with each model to support a fair comparison.
  • Record your voice during each interaction and pay close attention to the quality and behavior of the model's responses.
  • Evaluate each model across five defined evaluation dimensions.
  • Identify and categorize relevant error clusters that may occur in the audio or conversation.
  • Compare the performance of Model A and Model B based on the evaluation criteria and your observations.
  • Select the model that demonstrated the stronger overall performance according to the defined evaluation framework.
  • Write a detailed rationale explaining your final preference, referencing specific examples and observations from both conversations.
  • Apply evaluation guidelines consistently across different scenarios and model interactions

You’ll Thrive in This Role If You Have

  • Bachelors Degree
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to notice subtle differences in conversational quality.
  • Excellent listening and comprehension skills.
  • Strong written communication skills, particularly the ability to explain observations clearly and objectively.
  • Ability to follow detailed evaluation guidelines consistently.
  • Comfort speaking naturally and roleplaying different conversational scenarios.
  • Ability to compare two interactions fairly without allowing personal preferences to influence the evaluation.
  • Strong critical-thinking and analytical skills.
  • Reliability and consistency when completing structured evaluation tasks.
  • Familiarity with AI assistants, voice-based AI, or conversational systems

The expected hourly salary range for this position is $20-$27 p/hour, based on experience, skills, and qualifications.

title: Director, Quality
description:
About Us:

Toray Advanced Composites (TAC) is a leading supplier of advanced composite materials for the aerospace, sporting goods, motorsport, and industrial markets. You will find our thermoset composite products on nearly every satellite, space launch vehicle, unmanned aircraft, military and commercial aircraft in production today. TAC also provides composites materials to industrial and recreational applications including mountain bikes, medical prosthetics, and sports equipment.

Our thermoplastic prepregs, known in the industry as Cetex®, are found in a wide range of commercial and military aircraft, including large wing structures and interior applications like seats and galleys. Our Cetex products are available in unidirectional tape or fabric form in a variety of engineered thermoplastic resins including PEEK, PPS, PEI as well as a full line of performance thermoplastics including Nylon, PET, HDPE, and PP.


SUMMARY OF FUNCTIONS:

The Director of Quality will be responsible for leading and facilitating Toray’s TAC QA Systems and Lab activities across our 3 US locations. The Director will play an active role for the department by supporting the quality mission and focus on areas of improvement to ensure quality of products. As the quality director, this person will lead the strategic planning, coordination of Compliance, Risk Management, Quality, Improvement, and Innovation initiatives to our Aerospace and Defense products. Some of the areas of responsibility will include procurement standards, receiving inspection, manufacturing work instructions, testing, certification and shipment of composite materials and parts. This person will be a point of contact for the organization in investigating and setting standards for quality and analyzing the effectiveness of processes and quality management systems. Additionally, the Director, Quality will mentor and be an advocate for their team by supporting and providing feedback regarding their goals and accomplishments. Lastly this person will identify patterns of risky behavior within the organization and take appropriate action to resolve them and escalate serious issues as appropriate.

Please note roles and responsibilities are subject to change with or without advanced notice.

MAJOR DUTIES AND REQUIREMENTS

  • Serve as an executive and technical leader with responsibility for strategic planning, coordinating, and directing Compliance, Risk Management, Quality, Improvement, and Innovation initiatives to our Aerospace and Defense products.
  • Support the quality mission and focus on areas of improvement to ensure quality of products.
  • Partner with functional leaders across the organization to integrate “Built In Quality” into all levels and activities.
  • Serve as the advisor for government requirements regarding matters of compliance, risk management, safety, and quality for operations.
  • Develop and implement Advanced Quality Systems and quality control processes and procedures to ensure product quality and reliability.
  • Use data driven tools like Statistical Analysis, Statistical Process Control, capability analysis and Six Sigma to solve problems and promote critical thinking.
  • Ensure strategies/management systems are in place and ensure product quality meets the expectations of customers and stakeholders.
  • Must have a “Gemba Mindset” making frequent visits to the production and Quality Test lab areas building to build trust and encourage a quality mindset at the place work happens.
  • Plan, budget and execute resource needs to maintain an efficient but effective department for the both the lab and systems.
  • Responsible for the coaching and mentoring of the managers and supervisors in the Quality organization to ensure continued growth and development of a succession plan
  • Manage compliance to AS9100 and NADCAP certifications, including all aspects of the Quality Management system.
  • Responsible for internal audits, annual compliance and sustaining audits
  • Conduct quality audits and supplier evaluations to ensure compliance with standards and specifications.
  • Administer the document control and configuration management system.
  • Follow-up on and drive closure of Preventive and Corrective Action Request
  • Organize and coordinate the Material Review Board through the Catsweb system
  • Ensure that customer requests for Cause and Corrective Action are responded to in a timely manner and closed out to the customer’s satisfaction.
  • Support management in establishing and measuring process performance standards associated with quality, waste/throughput, customer satisfaction and productivity.
  • Develop and implement training programs to improve quality awareness and skills across the organization.
  • Provide input to operational reviews and other efforts leading to process improvements and cost reduction activities.
  • Support investigations and resolve operational non-conformances and customer related issues.
  • Participate in customer site audits and visits to Toray, support targeted projects in Toray or customer shops. Areas include defining and documenting product and processing parameters, capability, cost reductions, lean manufacturing, etc.
  • Work with leadership to drive the site goals and ensure the safe and environmentally sound performance of the site operations. The goal is to ensure that corporate and regulatory requirements are met or exceeded.
  • Work with leadership, implement actions that contribute to the goal of achieving financial targets, such as, productivity, throughput, and scrap levels and earnings.
  • Responsible for effectively managing, leading and creating/maintaining accountability of the Quality Department and team.
  • Ensure quarterly team S.M.A.R.T. goals are supporting company 1 year plan, 3-year and 10-year goal.
  • Accomplishes organization goals by accepting ownership for accomplishing new and different requests; exploring opportunities to add value to job accomplishments.
  • Serve as the point of contact for any escalations and provide support when needed to other TAC locations.

EXPERIENCE AND/OR EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Materials Science or related field required. Master’s Degree preferred.
  • Minimum of 12 years of experience working in quality implementation and management system ideally with composites or manufacturing.
  • Experience in an Aerospace focused organization combined with a demonstrated track-record of accomplishments as a Quality Assurance Manager or Supervisor
  • Experience with satisfying customers in technology-driven, progressive company.
  • Experience with FAA and international Quality System rules, regulations, including planning and implementation preferred.
  • Proven track record of leveraging continuous improvement and Kaizen methodologies to deliver business results.
  • Must be able to communicate clearly (written and verbally) in English.
  • Able to work and communicate with multiple teams.
  • Ability to motivate teams to produce high quality work product within tight timeframes and simultaneously manage several projects.
  • Proven leadership abilities, decisiveness in initiating actions
  • Able to develop, coach and motivate a team.
  • Ability to take initiative, to maintain confidentiality, to meet deadlines, and to work in a team environment.
  • PC-based computing experience (Word, Excel, Power Point, documentation s/w) essential.
  • Strategic thinker with strong analytical skills
  • Strong Process Orientation
  • Maintain work areas in a neat, orderly and safe manner.
  • Follow safety procedures for PPE (personal protection equipment)
  • Must be able to lift at least 20 pounds occasionally.

BENEFITS AND PERKS:

  • Comprehensive Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance Plans
  • FSA/HSA Plans Available
  • Paid Holidays
  • Gym Membership
  • Tuition Reimbursements
  • 401(k) Plan with Company Match
  • Paid Time Off, Paid Sick Leave
  • Employee Engagement Events
  • Referral Bonus Program
  • Life Insurance and AD&D Coverage
  • Short-Term and Long-Term Disability Insurance
  • Parental Leave & Paid Family Leave
  • Plus much more!


COMPENSATION: $175,000 - $205,000 yearly

title: Kennedy Shelter - Residential Coordinator (Sat/Sun, 8am-4pm)
description:
Title: Residential Coordinator
Level: Coordinator
Department: Kennedy Emergency Shelter
Reports to: Assistant Director of Shelter Operations
Pay Rate: $20/hour
Location: Fort Belvoir – Alexandria, VA
FLSA Status: Non-Exempt

About Us

Shelter House was established in 1981 as a grassroots responder to the homelessness crisis in Fairfax County. Since the organization’s inception, we have adapted and grown to meet community needs, all while working in partnership with government and private partners and community members. Today, Shelter House is a successful and reputable organization of over 200 employees committed to preventing and ending homelessness and domestic violence. In the last year, our compassionate team of individuals changed the lives of nearly 2,000 individuals, half of which were children. Our Culture is built from our Core Values of Inclusivity, Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, and Empowerment (iC.A.R.E.)

About the Role

The Residential Coordinator provides essential 24-hour awake coverage and supervision within our 50-bed shelter serving single adults. The Residential Coordinator serves as a first point of contact for client needs and support and plays an important role in maintaining a safe, supportive, and positive shelter environment.

This position is responsible for crisis intervention, front desk operations, facilities support, client assistance, and helping ensure the safe and efficient day-to-day operation of the shelter. The Residential Coordinator also helps ensure the safety of shelter residents and Shelter House property.

How You Will Contribute

  • Ensure the safe functioning of the shelter and maintain a safe and supportive environment for clients.
  • Monitor visitor check-in, front desk calls, and general inquiries.
  • Perform regular rounds and monitor the interior and exterior of the building and surrounding grounds.
  • Maintain the daily shelter log by documenting client interactions, incidents, and other significant events.
  • Work closely with Case Managers to support and reinforce client service plans and maintain ongoing communication regarding client progress.
  • Complete thorough shift exchanges with incoming and outgoing staff to maintain consistency and continuity of services.
  • Ensure shelter documentation is completed accurately and in accordance with agency policies and best practices.
  • Assess and respond to the basic needs of shelter clients while on shift, including distributing household items, toiletries, and other supplies as needed.
  • Perform residential cleaning duties, including light touch-ups and washing shelter linens.
  • Organize and restock household supplies, toiletries, linens, towels, and donations.
  • Perform unit inspections as required.
  • Maintain the dignity, privacy, and confidentiality of all clients throughout service delivery.
  • Maintain current knowledge of and ability to follow emergency procedures, including building evacuations, health emergencies, and safety protocols.
  • Accept donations and provide support for volunteer programs and shelter events.
  • Participate in staff meetings and trainings as directed.
  • Ensure compliance with all agency policies, procedures, and best practices.
  • Proficiently utilize Microsoft applications as part of day-to-day work responsibilities.
  • Serve as essential emergency personnel and report to work as scheduled during inclement weather and other emergency circumstances.
  • Exemplify Shelter House's core values (iC.A.R.E.): Inclusivity, Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, and Empowerment.
  • Perform other duties as necessary to support the program and agency.

Requirements

About You

Required Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • 2+ years of experience in the human services field, such as mental health, substance use services, homelessness services, or domestic violence services.
  • Ability to build strong working relationships with clients and team members.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Willingness to work evenings and weekends as needed.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in human services or a related field.
  • 1+ year of customer service experience.
  • Experience working in programs serving individuals or families experiencing homelessness.
  • Experience working in a residential environment.
  • Current CPR/First Aid certification.

Physical Requirements

  • Annual TB testing is required.
  • Ability to sit or stand for extended periods.
  • Ability to lift and carry items weighing approximately 10–20 pounds.

Benefits

Benefits:

  • Medical, Dental & Vision Insurance
  • 401K contributions with a 4% employer match
  • 13 Paid Holidays, 2 Floating Holidays and the opportunity to take your Birthday Off
  • Four Semi-Annual Team Building Events

Equal Employment Opportunity:

Equal Employment Opportunity Policy: Shelter House is committed to providing equal employment opportunity to all employees and applicants. All employment-related decisions will be made and carried out without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, age (over 40), sex, marital status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, disability unrelated to the individual's ability to perform his or her job or any other legally protected status. Shelter House will also provide reasonable accommodations to pregnant and qualified employees with disabilities to enable them to perform the essential functions of their job, and to employees with respect to their observance of their religious beliefs, in accordance with applicable law. Any job applicant or employee who would like or needs an accommodation may request an accommodation by contacting the Human Resources department.

Drug and Alcohol-Free Workplace Policy:

Drug-Free Workplace: Shelter House is committed to maintaining a drug-free workplace. Employment is contingent upon compliance with our Drug-Free Workplace Policy, which prohibits the unlawful manufacture, sale, distribution, dispensation, possession, or use of controlled substances or marijuana in the workplace. Additionally, all subcontracts and purchase orders over $10,000 must include provisions ensuring a drug-free workplace.

title: Team Lead, Software Development - 4
description:
Infor is seeking a Team Lead to guide a team of engineers delivering our AI-driven data migration and data governance platform, with python as the primary development language. This role blends hands-on technical leadership with people management — you'll set technical direction, remove delivery blockers, and grow your team's capabilities, while staying close enough to the code to make sound architectural calls and unblock hard problems. You'll partner with product managers, architects, and other team leads to translate business priorities into a healthy, well-executed engineering roadmap, including driving adoption of AI-assisted and agentic development practices across the team.
  • Set and enforce technical direction for the team's services, built primarily in Python, ensuring alignment with overall platform architecture.
  • Lead architecture discussions and design reviews for services deployed via Docker/Kubernetes on AWS.
  • Guide data modeling decisions across relational and document stores (PostgreSQL, DocumentDB), balancing team velocity with governance and data quality requirements.
  • Drive team-wide adoption of AI-assisted and agentic development tooling, establishing practices for how the team incorporates AI coding assistants and agentic workflows (agent orchestration, tool-use pipelines) into daily development — an area where Python is the dominant ecosystem.
  • Own delivery timelines and quality for the team's roadmap items, escalating risks early to product and engineering leadership.
  • Partner with product managers to scope work, estimate effort, and sequence priorities.
  • Coordinate with adjacent teams (architecture, DevOps, Java-based platform teams) to manage cross-team dependencies.
  • Maintain enough hands-on involvement in the codebase (Python, data pipelines, agent frameworks) to review critical designs and unblock hard technical problems.
  • Champion a polyglot approach, ensuring the team can flex into Java/Spring or other languages where existing platform services require it, even though Python is the team's primary language.

  • Hands-on background in Python, including experience building production services, data pipelines, or AI/agent-based tooling.
  • Prior experience leading or informally mentoring a team of engineers — technical lead, team lead, or equivalent.
  • Experience with AWS, Docker, and Kubernetes in production environments. Direct experience building or integrating AI-assisted or agentic development tooling (e.g., Claude Code, Copilot, Kiro , custom agent orchestration frameworks).
  • Experience with relational and document-oriented databases (PostgreSQL, DocumentDB or similar).
  • Polyglot proficiency — comfortable operating and guiding others across multiple languages (e.g., Python plus Java or JavaScript) as platform needs require.
  • Demonstrated ability to balance hands-on technical work with people-management responsibilities.
  • Experience with agentic pipeline design (orchestrator/agent patterns) for migration, automation, or data workflows.
