title: Lead Program Facilitator
description:
Lead Program Facilitator

POSITION SUMMARY

The Bay Area Discovery Museum is seeking a Lead Program Facilitator to join our Museum Experience team. This dynamic role facilitates and activates play-based learning programs, experiences, and environments, both onsite at the museum and in school and community settings. Lead Program Facilitators play a leadership role in guiding and catalyzing playful learning across museum programs including exhibits and festivals, school and community programs, and seasonal camps.

**We are particularly seeking bilingual candidates (fluent in English and Spanish, Cantonese, or Mandarin) in addition to candidates who are fluent in English and one of those additional specified languages.

Lead Program Facilitators bring a commitment to catalyzing and guiding playful learning that supports young children and their families to grow and thrive. They lead the activation of the museum floor and exhibits to create memorable and meaningful learning experiences for families with young children through planned and spontaneous playful interactions and games; open-ended questions and conversations that gently guide children’s play and model interactions for parent engagement; sharing information and suggestions with parents to enrich their families’ onsite experience and learning; and guiding Playful Learning Facilitators and Seasonal Playful Learning Assistants in their work to create a warm welcome and meaningful engagement for all visitors.

This position pays a rate of $27.24**/hour. This is a full-time union position, working 5 days per week onsite at our gorgeous 7.5-acre campus in Sausalito, CA. This position works Sunday-Thursday, with the possibility for one remote day a week. This role spends 95%+ of work time in a public-facing capacity on the museum floor.

**Bilingual candidates (fluent in English and Spanish, Mandarin, or Cantonese) will earn $28.24/hour.

KEY ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Museum Experience Floor, Support and Administration

  1. Leads the facilitation of daily museum drop-in onsite programs and such as Story Times, Pop Ups, Exhibit Activations, and Festivals.
  2. Participates in the development of, and delivers, special seasonal and year-round programs.
  3. Rotates through Museum Exhibits and engages in playful learning experiences with children and families.
  4. Facilitates programs in Spanish, Mandarin, or Cantonese, including translation of materials and communication (bilingual staff only).
  5. Works in partnership with other Playful Learning Facilitators and the Exhibits and Facilities team, to ensure that indoor and outdoor spaces are set up and maintained to be appealing, clean, and safe for all participants.
  6. Leads the daily opening and closing of museum exhibits in a complete and timely manner; Supports with daily closing announcements.
  7. Supports exhibits and programs with setup, clean-up and breakdown.
  8. Identifies and communicates material needs and exhibit/equipment repairs.
  9. Supports with trainings, leads and models programs and exhibit activations for Playful Learning Facilitators and Playful Learning Assistants.
  10. Participates in program ideation, prototyping, planning and evaluation, as required.
  11. Supports program administration and documentation with tasks such as organization of program supplies, creating program copy for Marketing, creating Program Signage as needed, creating Program Write Ups.
  12. Anticipates and problem solves day-of scheduling and other challenges, as appropriate.
  13. Supports as Floor Lead for the Museum Experience team one to two times per week.

Child and Adult Education

  1. Works in collaboration with the Child and Adult Education Department to lead the facilitation of Try It Truck Program in schools and community locations. This support takes place about twice a month.
  2. Trains to learn how to drive the Try It Truck, the museum’s mobile engineering lab.
  3. Motivates and guides playful learning; ensuring learning outcomes are met; activating teacher and parent engagement in the Try It Truck program, as appropriate.
  4. Facilitates programs in Spanish, Mandarin, or Cantonese, including translation of materials and communication (bilingual staff only)

Summer Camps

  1. Lead Program Facilitators support as one of several Camp Coordinators in the summer. This role supports summer camp leadership and staff, and coordinates program logistics. They are responsible for maintaining a positive and educational environment for campers and camp staff for designated seasonal camp sessions.
  2. Performs administrative duties, such as creating schedule rosters, maintaining inventory and restocking of supplies, preparing materials and other camp tasks.
  3. Supports with camp curriculum development.
  4. Assists with camp content training.
  5. Supports Senior and Junior Camp Facilitators on breaks and setting up activities. Serves as substitute Camp Facilitator as needed.
  6. Assists with addressing camper behavioral issues.
  7. Oversees and maintains museum supplies, equipment, and facilities. Manages camp lost and found.
  8. Participates in camp drop-off, pick-up, and written and verbal parent/caregiver communication.
  9. Works cooperatively to maintain open lines of communication with parents/caregivers, supervisors, and co-workers.
  10. Maintains a fun, positive, and friendly demeanor. Serves as an appropriate and positive role model for all campers, caregivers, and the general public.

Customer Service

  1. Ensures every visitor and program participant has an enjoyable experience, and feels welcome and taken care of, by providing exceptional customer service and communications centered in empathy, inclusion, and flexibility.
  2. Adheres to, communicates, and enforces museum policies and protocols around visitor safety and behavior.

SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS

  • 2+ years of experience working with children ages 0-8 years in formal or informal educational settings. Experience in education, arts education, early childhood education, museum studies, or relevant field preferred.
  • Understanding of early childhood development, pedagogy, and developmentally appropriate practice is preferred.
  • Ability to speak Spanish, Mandarin, or Cantonese is a plus.
  • Professional commitment to Diversity, Equity, Access, and Inclusion; thoughtful and open about the role of a workplace and a cultural institution in creating a sense of welcome and belonging for staff and visitors.
  • Excellent customer service skills.
  • Ability to take initiative, work independently, and troubleshoot in a fast-paced work environment.
  • Excellent oral, written, and interpersonal skills.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills, dependability, flexibility, and an outgoing and friendly personality.
  • Ability to work with a variety of people from various backgrounds and cultures.
  • Comfort speaking in front of large and small groups.
  • Ability to perform physical activities such as bending, kneeling, walking, and picking up items for 2-3 hours at a time. Ability to stand for up to 8 hours and carry up to 50 lbs. for short distances/periods. Ability to work indoors and outdoors in varying types of weather.
  • Must possess current driver’s license, have a clear Motor Vehicle Record, personal car insurance, and reliable access to a car as local travel is required.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

The Bay Area Discovery Museum is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity. We encourage those from all backgrounds to apply to allow us to build the most inclusive and creative team possible.

The Bay Area Discovery Museum is committed to being welcoming and inclusive. We are continuously working toward the goal of reflecting the diversity of the Bay Area both within our organization and with those we serve.

The Bay Area Discovery Museum offers a high-energy, results-oriented, creative and fun environment. Employees enjoy reciprocal admission benefits at other museums, regular all-staff celebrations, professional development training, and more. All staff members are valued for their contributions toward creating a high-quality experience for visitors, and their work that allows us to achieve our mission.

Staff working an average of 20+ hours per week are eligible for many of the same benefit plans on a prorated basis.

In addition, we offer the opportunity for each employee to make a unique impact on more than 350,000 museum visitors each year on-site, and many more in the community through the museum’s research-backed school and community programs.

title: Identity and Access Lead
description:
Life @ AP+

We are one connected team in pursuit of one inspiring purpose – to unite people and technology to power better experiences. Each of us has a part to play in making that happen. You’ll be encouraged to bring your big ideas forward and make a difference through your work. Taking steps forward in your career whilst still having room for fun, friendships, and flexibility in your daily life.

We’re driven by our core values: lead with heart, learn for tomorrow and live our legacy. A purpose like ours takes the inspired impact of an incredible team. Ready to change the game? We’re ready to help you do it.

The Purpose

As our Identity and Access Management Lead, you’ll help protect AP+ by making sure the right people have the right access to the right systems and data, at the right time. You’ll play a key role in establishing and continuously improving our Identity and Access Management (IAM) capability, helping reduce security risk while enabling our people and technology to operate securely and efficiently.

You’ll shape the frameworks, policies, standards and controls that underpin IAM across AP+, with a particular focus on identity lifecycle management, privileged access, authentication, authorisation and least-privilege access. You’ll work across technology, security and the broader business to embed secure access practices into platforms and services, while ensuring our controls remain aligned with organisational risk, compliance obligations and evolving security threats.

This role combines strategic thinking with practical delivery. You’ll oversee IAM control effectiveness, identify and remediate access risks and exceptions, support audits and risk assessments, and use data and reporting to provide clear insight into the effectiveness of our access controls. You’ll also help optimise and integrate IAM tooling, Identity Governance & Administration (IGA) and Privileged Access Management (PAM) solutions.

With identity sitting at the heart of modern security, you’ll help shape a scalable IAM capability that supports AP+ as it evolves, while providing specialist advice to technology and business teams on secure access patterns and how to protect critical systems and information.

Key Responsibilities the Role Owns

  • Define and maintain enterprise IAM policies, standards, controls and the target-state IAM roadmap.
  • Oversee identity lifecycle processes, including joiner, mover and leaver management, access provisioning and de-provisioning.
  • Manage Privileged Access Management (PAM) governance, controls and continuous improvement.
  • Ensure authentication, authorisation and access control designs align with security risk and compliance requirements.
  • Partner with security engineering, operations and architecture teams to embed IAM controls into platforms and services.
  • Monitor and report on IAM control effectiveness, access exceptions and compliance obligations, driving remediation where required.
  • Lead IAM-related risk assessments, audits and evidence management for internal and external stakeholders.
  • Drive the configuration, optimisation and integration of IAM tooling, including Identity Governance & Administration (IGA) and Privileged Access Management (PAM) solutions.
  • Support the investigation and response to access-related security incidents and suspected credential misuse.
  • Provide specialist advice to technology and business teams on secure access patterns, identity governance and least privilege.

You’ll likely be a strong fit for this role if

You’re an experienced IAM or PAM professional who enjoys solving complex security challenges and building practical controls that protect an organisation without getting in the way of good business outcomes. You’ll bring demonstrated experience leading IAM capabilities in a complex enterprise environment, with strong knowledge of identity governance, privileged access management, and least-privilege principles.

You’ll be comfortable working across security, technology and business teams, providing specialist advice and influencing how identity and access controls are designed and implemented. Experience supporting audits, risk assessments and control uplift initiatives will be important, along with an understanding of security risk management and relevant standards and regulatory obligations. Relevant certifications across platforms will be valuable, but strong practical experience will be equally important.

What happens next

At AP+, we believe in the power of passion, pride and purpose. Our team is driven by a shared mission to make a difference in the world of payments, and we're proud to work together towards this common goal.

If you’re an Identity and Access Management professional who enjoys solving complex security challenges, strengthening controls and helping organisations operate securely, we’d love to hear from you.

If you’re ready to be a game changer, please submit your application. The Talent Acquisition team will endeavor to review your application and notify you of the outcome within the next two weeks.

We want to remove all barriers to inclusion, so if you need advice or support with your application, we’re here to help. Please reach out to recruitment@auspayplus.com.au. We also encourage you to let us know your pronouns at any point during the recruitment process.

AP+ are not partnering with Recruitment agencies for this role.

title: Head of HSEQ, Risk & Business Transformation
description:
Job Description

Head of HSEQ, Risk & Business Transformation

Overview

Enemix is working with our client, a progressive head contractor specializing in electrical infrastructure projects, to identify an outstanding professional for this transformative role. Our client's culture is built on trust, safety, and quality—key pillars for delivering successful projects.

This is not a traditional HSEQ role.

As our client enters the next phase of growth, they are seeking a senior leader to take full ownership of their HSEQ, risk, governance, and business systems framework. With the foundations already being established, your role will be to make these systems operational, embed accountability across the organization, and ensure the framework is practical, consistently followed, and well understood. Once established, you will lead the next stage of improvement in systems, processes, digital platforms, data, and overall business performance.

Responsibilities

As the Head of HSEQ, Risk & Business Transformation, you will lead:

  • HSEQ, risk, and governance initiatives.
  • Management systems, compliance, and assurance programs.
  • Contractor and project assurance processes.
  • Incident management and organizational learning frameworks.
  • HSEQ reporting, data analysis, and performance tracking.
  • Leadership capability development and accountability measures.
  • Continuous improvement and business transformation projects.
  • Digital platforms, integration, and systems improvement.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will collaborate closely with executives, project teams, engineers, supervisors, and field personnel to seamlessly integrate HSEQ principles into the daily operations—not as a standalone function but as a core business priority.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

  • Improve and maintain the management system in line with ISO 45001, ISO 14001, and ISO 9001 standards.
  • Lead the internal audit and assurance program.
  • Serve as the primary contact for certification bodies, clients, regulators, and auditors.
  • Oversee the end-to-end incident management framework, from conducting investigations to embedding lessons learned.
  • Design and implement a structured continuous improvement framework across the organization.
  • Evaluate and implement digital platforms that synchronize systems, reduce duplication, enhance data visibility, and centralize critical information.

Qualifications

Essential:
  • Relevant tertiary qualification in Quality, Health & Safety, Environmental Management, Risk, Engineering, Business, Project Management, or a related discipline.
  • Proven senior experience in QSE or HSEQ management.
  • In-depth knowledge of ISO 9001, ISO 14001, and ISO 45001, as well as OFSC criteria.
  • Demonstrable success in implementing, maintaining, and refining integrated management systems.
  • Exceptional expertise in risk management and assurance.
  • Experience in developing governance frameworks, business processes, and procedures.
  • Proficiency in incident management, including investigation and corrective action planning.
  • Strong leadership and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Excellent written and oral communication abilities.
  • A strategic mindset with the ability to remain operationally focused when needed.
Preferred:
  • Industry experience in electrical, utilities, energy, construction, infrastructure, or transmission and distribution environments.
  • Familiarity with OFSC accreditation, Principal Contractor environments, or high-risk, large-scale construction projects.
  • Experience with digital system enhancements, ERP platforms, or HSEQ digital tools.

Your First 12 Months

This role comes with the flexibility to tailor your approach. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to present a 3, 6, and 12-month roadmap to outline their strategies and priorities. This process will help our client understand your thought process, leadership style, and approach to challenges.

Additionally, you will have the unique opportunity to design the future structure of the department, identify areas for development, and build a team to drive sustained growth. With a firm foundation in place, you will play a key role in shaping a high-impact function.

What Success Looks Like

  • Business leaders take full ownership of their risks and responsibilities.
  • The HSEQ framework is practical, widely understood, and consistently applied across the organization.
  • HSEQ is recognized as a driver of performance rather than a compliance function.
  • Governance improves decision-making and operational transparency.
  • Efficient, scalable systems are effectively deployed.
  • Key lessons from incidents and assurance programs inform continuous improvements.
  • Digital tools improve efficiency, reduce administrative duplication, and enhance data visibility.
  • The HSEQ function earns credibility and is respected for its strategic and operational impact.

Benefits

  • Lead and transform a critical function within a growing organization.
  • Excellent remuneration package with flexibility based on value, responsibilities, and outcomes.
  • Opportunities for flexible working arrangements after the first 12–18 months.
  • Regular travel opportunities to construction sites across NSW and Victoria, and potentially nationwide.
  • Make an impact through the ability to build and lead a team, shaping the future of the HSEQ function.

Location & Travel

The position will initially be based at our client’s office just outside of Sydney CBD, with frequent travel to construction sites across NSW and Victoria. As the business grows, there may be opportunities for national travel. Regular site visits are required to engage with teams, foster relationships, and establish credibility with project and field personnel.

Why This Role?

This is your opportunity to take ownership and drive transformation. With the foundation in place, you can work with our client to build and embed robust systems, lead continuous improvement, and contribute to their ongoing success and expansion.

If you are a forward-thinking, motivated professional looking to create meaningful impact through innovation and leadership, we encourage you to apply.

_For more information on this incredible opportunity to join a growing and progressive organization, contact us at Enemix.

title: Senior Data Pipeline Engineer/Developer
description:
Position Overview

We are seeking a Senior Data Pipeline Engineer/Developer to design, build, and own the data pipelines that move genomic and operational data from lab instruments and LIMS through to analytics, products, and clinical reporting. In this senior individual-contributor role you will set technical direction for our data platform, build production pipelines that are reliable and reproducible at scale, and provide architectural and code-level guidance to existing engineering teams. You will own data quality, lineage, and observability end to end, and operate in a regulated environment where reproducibility and auditability are non-negotiable. This is a Python-first, full-stack engineering role. This is a contractor position, slated for a 12-month term.


Accountabilities and Responsibilities

  • Pipeline Engineering & Integration
    • Builds and operates production ETL and ELT for high-volume genomic data as well as operational and business data.
    • Integrates data across LIMS, lab instruments, internal applications, and third-party sources through robust, well-tested interfaces.
    • Develops across the stack in Python (data services, internal APIs, and supporting application code) and provides architectural and code-level guidance to engineering teams on data-layer integration.
  • Architecture & Technical Leadership
    • Sets technical direction for batch and streaming data pipelines by evaluating frameworks, orchestration, storage, and processing patterns, making recommendations, and leading adoption.
    • Models and tunes data stores (Microsoft SQL Server and PostgreSQL, plus a cloud warehouse or lake) for performance and scale.
    • Defines and enforces engineering standards for testing, CI/CD, infrastructure as code, code review, and architecture decision records.
  • Data Quality & Pipeline Observability
    • Owns data quality, lineage, and observability, including freshness, completeness, schema-drift detection, cost-per-job, and SLAs.
    • Builds pipelines for reproducibility and audit-readiness, incorporating versioned data and code, lineage, decision logging, access controls, and evidence collection.
    • Partners with security and compliance on data privacy, PII and PHI handling, and regulatory requirements across the data lifecycle.
  • Regulatory Compliance and Security Governance
    • Apply deep understanding of CAP/CLIA, HIPAA, GDPR, and GxP regulations specifically to data pipeline architecture.
    • Oversee protected health information (PHI) handling, data lineage, retention, and comprehensive audit logging.
    • Produce and maintain the critical operational evidence required to carry the data platform successfully through compliance audits.
    • Adhere to strict data-governance controls necessary for securely handling sensitive genomic data across global regions.
    • Enforce least-privilege access and ensure zero data egress to personal or unapproved infrastructure.
    • Utilize exclusively de-identified or synthetic data within development environments.
    • Maintain strict compliance with international data-residency and localization requirements.


Position Requirements

  • Skills and Knowledge
    • Strong SQL proficiency on Microsoft SQL Server and PostgreSQL, including schema design, query tuning, and performance troubleshooting.
    • Strong Python proficiency across the stack (data pipelines, backend services, and APIs). This is a Python-first role.
    • Production experience with a workflow orchestrator (Argo Workflows, Step Functions, Prefect, Dagster, Airflow, or similar).
    • Production experience with containers (Docker) and Kubernetes, which the lead orchestrator (Argo Workflows) runs on.
    • Strong testing discipline, including unit, integration, and data-quality or contract tests.
    • Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain data tradeoffs to technical and compliance stakeholders.
    • Genomics or NGS data formats and handling (FASTQ, BAM/CRAM, VCF).

title: Principal Customer and Network Advisor
description:
Cross River Rail Delivery Authority (CRRDA)…Your chance to work with the best!


The Cross River Rail Delivery Authority is building a new 10.2km rail line that includes 5.9km of twin tunnels running under the Brisbane River and CBD; with four new underground stations at Boggo Road, Woolloongabba, Albert Street and Roma Street.


Once complete, it will provide trains with a much-needed alternative rail path through the core of the current SEQ Rail network, unlocking a bottleneck and allowing more trains to run more often across the whole of South East Queensland.


The Cross River Rail Delivery Authority is also delivering multiple supporting projects and activities in conjunction with the Department of Transport and Main Roads. These include accessibility rebuilds for eight surface stations, construction of three new stations on the Gold Coast; upgrades for stabling yards; track works and surface rail enhancements; and the introduction of a new ETCS digital signalling system.



About the Role


The Principal Customer & Network Advisor plays a critical role in preparing organisations, stakeholders and operating environments for the successful introduction of major project outcomes across the Cross River Rail program.


The position is responsible for leading readiness initiatives associated with new infrastructure, operational capability, network changes, timetable changes, station openings and other significant project milestones. The role operates across complex, multi-agency environments and requires the ability to coordinate stakeholders, manage risks and dependencies, and drive outcomes through collaboration and influence.


This role provides a unique opportunity to contribute to some of South East Queensland's most significant transport initiatives, supporting the transition from construction and testing through to operational implementation and opening. This opportunity is offered as a fixed term contract until March 2029 .



Key Responsibilities:



  • Lead and coordinate readiness activities associated with new infrastructure, operational capability, network changes, timetable changes, station openings and other major project outcomes

  • Manage risks, issues, dependencies and interfaces associated with readiness and implementation activities

  • Coordinate stakeholders across government agencies, operators, delivery partners and project teams to support successful implementation outcomes

  • Develop readiness strategies, implementation plans, governance artefacts and assurance activities to support project delivery

  • Analyse technical information and identify customer, operational and network impacts to inform readiness planning and decision-making

  • Develop and maintain governance frameworks, project controls and reporting for operational, executive and decision-making audiences

  • Lead readiness workshops, governance forums and planning activities to support stakeholder alignment and effective decision-making

  • Support implementation and day-of-operations activities associated with major project milestones and service transitions



About You:


This role will suit a professional with experience in readiness planning, operational change, program delivery, project implementation, transport operations or major infrastructure programs. You will be recognised for your ability to bring multiple stakeholders together, navigate complexity and drive delivery outcomes through collaboration and influence.


You will ideally demonstrate:



  • Strong understanding of public transport operations, readiness planning, organisational change or major project implementation activities

  • Experience maintaining governance, program management and reporting frameworks

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to translate complexity into practical recommendations

  • Strong stakeholder engagement, negotiation and influencing skills

  • Proven ability to identify risks, issues, dependencies and opportunities and develop practical mitigation strategies

  • The ability to adapt quickly to changing priorities in a complex and evolving delivery environment




Why work with CRRDA?


On Cross River Rail you will not only work with the best but become your best. And as we enter a new phase of delivery, our project offers a rare career opportunity for top tier professionals to have played their part on something that is genuinely city shaping and transformative.


Our people are supported with flexible work options, career development through the Australian Institute of Management, salary packaging and access to world class employee assistance provider Telus Health.


At Cross River Rail we are an equal opportunity employer and strive to build balanced teams from all walks of life.



How To Apply


Please submit your Resume by clicking on the apply link before the closing date of 5 October 2026.


Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people are strongly encouraged to apply for all Cross River Rail Delivery Authority vacancies.

About us

The Greyhound Welfare & Integrity Commission is an independent statutory body established under the Greyhound Racing Act 2017. The Commission is responsible for promoting and protecting the welfare of greyhounds, safeguarding the integrity of greyhound racing and betting, and maintaining public confidence in the NSW greyhound racing industry.

As a trusted, fair, firm and impartial regulator, the Commission plays an important role in supporting a safe, compliant and sustainable greyhound racing industry in NSW. Our work is focused on high standards of welfare and integrity, effective regulation, intelligence-led decision-making and strong stakeholder engagement

About the role

We have an exciting opportunity for a Data Analytics & Intelligence Analyst to join the Commission’s Racing Integrity Team. This role delivers data-led intelligence and analytical support to inform investigations, compliance activity and operational decision-making across the Commission.

In this role, you will interrogate and interpret information from multiple sources, identify patterns, trends, risks and associations, and produce clear intelligence products, reports, graphs and trend analyses. You will also support ongoing investigations and compliance operations through the development of intelligence profiles, targeted analytical products and evidence-based insights.

This is a unique opportunity to apply your data analytics, intelligence and reporting skills in a regulatory environment where your work will directly support greyhound welfare, racing integrity and public confidence in the industry.

What you’ll do:

  • Collect, collate, analyse and interpret intelligence and data to support investigations, compliance functions and organisational decision-making.
  • Develop clear, accurate and evidence-based intelligence reports, assessments, briefs, research papers, graphs and trend analyses.
  • Use data analytics and intelligence tools, including Tableau or similar platforms, to identify trends, risks, associations and emerging issues.
  • Support operational investigations and compliance activities by preparing intelligence profiles and targeted analytical products.
  • Work collaboratively with internal teams and external stakeholders to support information sharing, intelligence objectives and continuous improvement.
  • Maintain confidentiality, integrity and security of information in a complex and sensitive regulatory environment.

About You

We are looking for a motivated and analytical professional who can work confidently with complex information, identify meaningful insights and communicate findings clearly to support investigations, compliance and regulatory decision-making.

To be successful in this role, you will bring:

  • Demonstrated experience working as a data, business or intelligence analyst, preferably in a law enforcement, regulatory, compliance or investigative environment.
  • Strong capability in data analysis, intelligence analysis, research and reporting, including the ability to draw insights from multiple information sources.
  • The ability to prepare clear, concise and accurate written products for operational, investigative and executive audiences.
  • Sound judgement, discretion and professionalism when handling confidential, sensitive or operational information.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to manage competing priorities in a high-volume, time-sensitive environment.

Essential requirements

  • Relevant tertiary qualifications (Intelligence Analysis, Data Analytics, Criminology or similar) or equivalent experience.
  • Appointment is subject to the successful completion of all pre-employment checks, including criminal record, employment and referee checks, and the assessment of any matters that may present a conflict with the Commission's integrity and regulatory functions, including betting and wagering activities.

title: Computer Science & Computer Vision AI/ML Intern
description:
THE MISSION

ITERRA is building the system of record for low-altitude airspace.

Above 400 feet, every aircraft is tracked, logged, and attributable. Transponders, flight plans, radar, ATC. Below it, nothing. No transponder mandate an adversary obeys, no log, no attribution. Every headline ends the same way: nobody could say what was in that airspace.

A record-keeper cannot be a participant in the fight it is recording. That is why we are passive, and it is not a limitation, it is the product.

WHAT WE ARE BUILDING

Passive, edge-native RF and electro-optical sensing that autonomously detects and classifies Group 1-3 UAS without relying on pre-loaded signature libraries. Fused on the device. No active emissions. No cloud dependency. Purpose-built for denied, degraded, intermittent, and limited (DDIL) environments where legacy radar and library-dependent sensors fail.

WHO WE ARE

Small team. High trust. No bureaucracy. No tourists. Only builders.

Field-tested, integrated with the command-and-control systems our customers already run, SDVOSB certified, and manufacturing on U.S. soil in Hatillo, Puerto Rico.

WHAT YOU OWN

The sensor hears a drone before anyone sees it. Your job is the part that turns what it hears, and what the cameras see, into a call the operator can act on. You own a real slice of the perception stack, with your own dates, alongside the engineers. You report to the CTO.

  • Computer vision on the edge. Detection and tracking of Group 1-3 airframes in visible and infrared imagery. Training, evaluation, and the honest confusion matrix that comes with them. Small, fast, low-power models, not leaderboard models. The electro-optical and infrared line is a development track, not a shipped product, and you would be working on it from the beginning.
  • Deployment on NVIDIA Jetson. Getting a model off your laptop and onto the unit: quantization, TensorRT, throughput and latency measured on the actual board under Caribbean heat, not estimated.
  • Dataset and labeling pipeline. Collection, labeling protocol, versioning, augmentation, train and validation splits that do not leak. The training corpus is a company asset and you help build it.
  • Field data capture. You come to the range. Live airframes, fixed and moving, multiple types. You help run the collection and you carry the gear.
  • Evaluation you would defend. Precision, recall, false alarm rate, and the conditions each was measured under. Written so it can drop into a federal proposal without rewriting.
  • Fusion with the RF side. Working with the RF engineer so that what the antenna detects and what the camera sees agree on a single track. Both halves are passive. The system listens and looks; it never transmits.
  • Tooling. The small scripts, dashboards, and harnesses that make the above repeatable by someone who is not you.

The model you ship is the model that runs on the unit in the field. Nobody downstream second-guesses it. That is the weight of the seat.

HOW WE WORK

We are small, and we move at a pace that only a small team can. Engineering runs on two-week cycles against a single shared plan. Every seat, RF, mechanical, electrical, and software, owns a slice of the same rig and has to land its objectives on the same date the others do. An antenna that is finished three weeks before the enclosure is not finished. A mount that is finished after the field test is a failure.

You scope your own work, commit to dates, say early and loudly when a date is at risk, and integrate with the rest of the stack instead of handing over a part and walking away. Pace is a requirement of the seat, not a culture slogan, and it is the reason a company our size can put fielded hardware in front of a government customer.

WHAT WE REQUIRE

Pursuing or holding a B.S. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field. This is an early-career seat and we expect to teach you things. What we cannot teach in six months is whether you build. Hands-on work counts wherever you did it: thesis, senior design, student competition, a personal project, or a bench in your apartment. We care that you have done it, not who paid you to.

  • You have trained a model and looked hard at where it failed. Any domain. Tell us what the model got wrong, why, and what you changed. A project where everything worked tells us nothing.
  • Python, working fluency. NumPy, and PyTorch or TensorFlow. You can read someone else's repository and get it running.
  • Computer vision fundamentals. Convolutional networks, object detection and tracking, data augmentation, overfitting, the difference between validation and test. OpenCV.
  • Linux comfort. Shell, ssh, git. You can work on a headless machine without a GUI.
  • You finish things. One project, start to finish, that you can put on a screen and walk us through. Coursework counts. So does a bench in your apartment.
  • Willing to be outside. Field days are part of this seat, not an exception to it.
  • Juvempleo eligibility. Ages 18 to 29, Puerto Rico resident, U.S. citizen, minimum 2.00 GPA, recently graduated or about to graduate. Placement is made by DDEC, not by ITERRA alone.
  • Method over conclusions. If the measurement says the product underperforms, we need to hear it from you first, and we will act on it, not argue with it.
  • U.S. person under ITAR.
  • Onsite in Hatillo, Puerto Rico, and in the field, outdoors, carrying gear.

Preferred: multi-object tracking. EO/IR or thermal imagery. Model optimization (TensorRT, ONNX, quantization, pruning). ROS. C++. Drone or UAS hands-on time. Clearance eligibility. Spanish.

WHAT WE OFFER

This seat is funded through Juvempleo, the Departamento de Desarrollo Economico y Comercio youth employment program. DDEC carries the wage. What ITERRA gives you is the work itself.

  • $15.00 per hour, paid through Juvempleo. 950 hours, roughly six months.
  • Real hardware from week one. You are not shadowing anybody. You get a slice of the rig, a date, and the same standard of review the engineers get.
  • Direct access to the CTO and the founder. No layers. Your work is reviewed by the people who will ship it.
  • Your work goes to the field. Whatever you build gets carried outside, mounted, and run against live targets while you are still here. Very few engineers get that before their first full-time job.
  • A portfolio you can show anybody. Code, measurements, and a documented result you were responsible for, on a fielded defense system built in Puerto Rico.
  • First look at a full-time seat. We hire from this bench. Performing here is the shortest path onto the payroll.

ITERRA sets compensation based on demonstrated capability, role scope, and specialized skill sets, including active security clearances. Positions may also be eligible for equity in iTerra Solutions, Inc. and company-sponsored health benefits. Specific eligibility is confirmed at offer.

Expected Base Salary Range
$15—$15 USD

This position requires access to export-controlled information under ITAR (22 CFR 120-130). Applicants must be U.S. persons as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3).

ITERRA is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

title: Data Engineer Payments & Funds-Flow
description:
About the Role OSL Group is a listed digital-asset and fintech group; Banxa is our regulated crypto payments and fiat on/off-ramp business. This role is the data owner for the payments and funds-flow domain, serving the payments, finance, compliance and risk teams. Core stack is MaxCompute and DataWorks with CDC-based ingestion. The role works in an AI-native way by default.

What We're Really Looking For We care more about how you think and the leverage you create than about any specific tool. Modelling judgement.

You turn messy, multi-source payment flows into clean, reusable models, and can defend your choices on grain, dimensions and trade-offs. You've owned at least one subject area end to end. Correctness under compliance.

You treat financial data as something that must reconcile and survive audit — idempotent, precise, verifiable — not just 'loaded'. Ownership over ambiguity.

You engage upstream at product kick-off, pin down definitions before writing code, and stay accountable from ingestion to the business outcome rather than stopping at your layer. Influence without authority.

You get backend, SRE, finance and compliance teams to move with you, and you set the quality bar and SLAs for a domain rather than following someone else's. AI-native leverage.

Strong SQL and dimensional modelling, with end-to-end ownership of at least one subject area. Production CDC ingestion experience, including late and out-of-order events, deduplication, soft deletes and schema evolution. Accuracy engineering for financial data: idempotent writes, numeric precision, reconciliation and cross-system consistency checks. Agent-based development capability: multi-step agent workflows, tool and data-source integration through MCP, and reusable skills; context engineering, tool-call design, agent evaluation and debugging. Ownership of a data quality framework, covering rule design, threshold rationale, alert response and SLA commitments. Preferred Crypto or digital-asset data experience: on/off-ramp, on-chain or stablecoin settlement, multi-asset exposure. Multi-timezone, multi-currency and multi-region data, including business-day cut-off, FX treatment and localisation. Financial audit or regulatory-reporting support, including source-of-truth and explainable change history. Cross-engine migration experience, for example MaxCompute or Hadoop to Snowflake or Databricks. Building metadata, lineage, catalogue, metric platforms — or

AI data agents / LLM-powered tooling . Python or Java for internal tooling and services. Familiarity with compliance constraints on architecture: PCI DSS, GDPR, data localisation, row and column level security, masking. How We Work Definitional rigour

— clarify before you code. Reproducible by default

— idempotent, re-runnable, verifiable. End-to-end ownership

— own the full chain and faces the business directly. AI-native

— highest-leverage path first; automate the routine, keep human judgement where correctness and compliance demand it.

location: UCP Immersive Learning Academy - Orlando, FL 32817
description:
Looking to make a difference in an innovative and dynamic inclusive charter school network? UCP Charter Schools are a network of 8 PreK-12th grade schools for students with and without disabilities in Central Florida.

UCPs instructional approach is designed to reach every learner through customized instruction, technology integration, art integration, and project-based learning. Each UCP campus has a unique community feel, with low student/instructor ratios and inclusive classrooms where children with and without disabilities learn and grow together.

Job Summary:
The Principal of Innovation and New School Development serves as the instructional and operational leader for UCP Charter Schools' emerging educational initiatives. During the 2026–2027 school year, this position will provide leadership for the UCP Immersive Learning Charter Academy (Virtual School) while leading the planning, development, approval, staffing, and launch of the UCP Career Academy.
This role is ideal for an entrepreneurial educational leader who enjoys building programs from the ground up, solving complex challenges, and creating innovative learning opportunities for students. As both schools mature, organizational responsibilities may evolve based on enrollment, operational needs, and the strengths and interests of the successful candidate.
This position is designed to support the launch and growth of two strategic initiatives: the UCP Immersive Learning Charter Academy (Virtual School) and the UCP Career Academy. As enrollment and organizational needs evolve, responsibilities may be adjusted. Following the successful launch period, the Superintendent may assign the position to continue leading one of these schools or another strategic initiative based on organizational priorities and the strengths and interests of the successful candidate.

Primary Responsibilities

Virtual School Leadership

  • Serve as Principal of the UCP Immersive Learning Charter Academy.
  • Ensure compliance with Florida virtual education requirements and charter school expectations.
  • Hire/train and supervise school-based staff
  • Monitor student achievement, attendance, engagement, and progress.
  • Build strong relationships with students and families.
  • Oversee school culture and student support systems.
  • Coordinate state testing and accountability requirements.
  • Monitor enrollment growth and retention.
  • Collaborate with curriculum, ESE, assessment, technology, and operations departments.

Career Academy Development

Lead the planning and launch of UCP's new Career Academy, including:

Program Design

  • Develop the educational vision and instructional model.
  • Design school systems and operational procedures.
  • Collaborate on curriculum development and career pathways.
  • Develop student support systems.
  • Build industry partnerships.

Charter Implementation

  • Ensure implementation of charter commitments.
  • Assist with compliance reporting.
  • Develop policies and operational procedures.
  • Coordinate opening timelines.

Staffing

  • Assist with recruiting and hiring faculty and staff.
  • Develop onboarding plans.
  • Create professional learning systems.
  • Build school culture before opening.

Enrollment

  • Support student recruitment efforts.
  • Participate in marketing and community outreach.
  • Develop family engagement strategies.
  • Collaborate with enrollment specialists.

Operations

  • Coordinate with Facilities regarding campus readiness.
  • Assist with furniture, technology, and equipment planning.
  • Develop master schedules.
  • Coordinate opening logistics.

Leadership Responsibilities

  • Foster a positive, inclusive school culture aligned with UCP's mission.
  • Lead continuous school improvement efforts.
  • Analyze student performance data.
  • Supervise and evaluate staff.
  • Ensure implementation of MTSS.
  • Maintain compliance with all federal, state, and local requirements.
  • Collaborate closely with district leadership.

What UCP Offers

Our mission at UCP is to empower children with and without disabilities to achieve their potential by providing individualized support, education and therapy services in an inclusive environment. When you join UCP of Central Florida you partner with a team that is making a positive impact on the futures of our children. For over 70 years, we have been dedicated to enriching the lives of children of all abilities across Central Florida. We provide individualized Support, Education, and Therapy services to thousands of children at 8 campuses in: Downtown Orlando, East Orlando (near UCF), Kissimmee, Pine Hills, Lake Mary, and Winter Garden.

UCP of Central Florida offers a competitive benefit package available to all employees! Some perks to being a UCP Team Member may include: health insurance (free option after the first year), dental insurance options, free life insurance, paid time off, discounted on-site childcare, 403B/Retirement match, short & long term disability, and support in continuing your education.

title: Senior Enterprise Architect (Associate, Contract)
description:
Intelance works with UK organisations that need clear, practical decisions about technology. We are building a trusted group of senior associates to lead short enterprise architecture engagements. This project based contract role is for someone who can understand how decisions are made, find where ownership or information is unclear, and give senior leaders a plan they can use.

Tasks

You will:

  • Lead current state enterprise architecture reviews from the first interview to the executive readout.
  • Interview senior business and technology leaders, then explain the findings in plain English.
  • Map how decisions are made across applications, data, integration, security, operations and change.
  • Test early findings against real decisions, documents and other evidence.
  • Identify unclear ownership, duplicated effort, avoidable risk and important dependencies.
  • Design practical options, clear decision rights and a costed roadmap.
  • Produce board ready reports, diagrams and presentations.
  • Work with Intelance associates while owning the quality of the work and the client relationship.

Requirements

You must have:

  • At least 10 years of enterprise architecture, business architecture or technology governance experience.
  • Personally led a current state assessment from discovery through to an executive readout.
  • Experience interviewing and presenting to Board, COO, CIO or equivalent leaders.
  • Strong knowledge of applications, data, integration, security, operating models and technology governance.
  • Recent work in a law firm, professional services partnership, financial services firm or another regulated organisation.
  • Evidence that you can turn complex findings into clear written advice and practical decisions.
  • The confidence to challenge senior people calmly and work without depending on a large consulting team.
  • The right to work and contract in the UK without sponsorship.
  • Availability for remote work and occasional travel to London or other UK client sites.
  • The ability to meet Intelance checks for conflicts, references, confidentiality, information security and insurance.

TOGAF or a similar qualification is useful, but clear evidence of delivery matters more.

Benefits

  • £700 to £850 per day, excluding VAT, based on experience and the scope of each assignment.
  • Project based associate contract with no guaranteed minimum number of days.
  • Initial assignments are usually 10 to 20 days delivered over three to six weeks.
  • Mostly remote work with planned UK client travel when needed.
  • Direct access to the senior people making the decisions.
  • Further work may follow across enterprise architecture, AI governance, data and security.

Apply if you can lead the work yourself and produce clear outputs for senior leaders. We will review your application, hold a short fit call, and then complete references, conflict and contracting checks. We will not ask you to write a long unpaid proposal.

This is a unique opportunity for you to join the Reserve Bank’s Payments Operations Program, which is leading the Bank's work to strengthen its operation of RITS, Australia's real-time gross settlement system, and other critical national payments infrastructure. These payments systems move around $300 billion dollars between financial institutions each day and ultimately settle all non-cash payments in Australia. They are essential for supporting the day-to-day business of the Australian economy.

You will be part of the Knowledge Management team in the Payments Operations Program, working closely with other members of the workstream and subject matter experts in IT and Payments Settlements departments to uplift the Bank's key knowledge artefacts for the RITS ecosystem.

  • You will also enjoy working and collaborating with multiple high performing teams committed to team goals and deliverables

  • Experience working in cross-functional teams including IT, operations, risk and compliance
